column5: After a long and bloody series of matches, a new leader was appointed.\nAlarinthia remained unchanged — always in the hands of the mighty.\nIt would stay that way, until somebody else got the courage to rise up.
column6: 经过漫长而血腥的连番较量，新的领袖被推选出来。\n阿拉林西亚依旧如故——始终掌握在强者手中。\n这种局面会一直持续下去，直到有人鼓起勇气揭竿而起。

column5: The Created Seers seemed to be affected by your attack on the dark idol.\nAs if offering their strength when needed the most, the energy within them vanished.\nWhen the fog of war settled, they were no longer plagued with visions. They had healthy minds.
column6: 你袭击黑暗灵像的举动，似乎影响到了那些被创造出的先知。\n仿佛在最需要的时刻献出了自己的力量，他们体内的能量就此消散。\n当战火平息，他们不再被幻象折磨，心智恢复了健全。

column5: A small ceremony was held to mourn and honor the sacrifice of your Created Seers.\nThough their life on Alestia was short — they had completed enough to be known as heroes.\nBut many wondered what would've happened if they survived. Could their minds have been saved?
column6: 人们举行了一场小小的仪式，悼念并致敬你那些被创造出的先知的牺牲。\n尽管他们在阿莱斯蒂亚的生命很短暂——但他们的成就已足以被誉为英雄。\n但许多人不禁想，若他们活下来会怎样。他们的心智还能被拯救吗？

column5: After the chaos dwindled, Nada returned to Mazeo to retrieve her end of the bargain.\nEvery pirate was forgiven for their crimes, and followed Nada to her new, powerful nation.\nWith trade bans lifted, her new nation quickly became more powerful than Mazeo.
column6: 混乱平息后，娜达回到马泽奥，索取她应得的那份报酬。\n每一名海盗的罪行都被赦免，他们追随娜达，投奔了她那崭新的强国。\n随着贸易禁令解除，她的新国家迅速变得比马泽奥更为强大。

column5: The Mazean Shipping Company simply couldn't compete with such skilled individuals.\nThe discretion and speed associated with working a life of crime gave her team the advantage.\nShe eventually amassed enough to purchase the company, and she dominated the industry.
column6: 马泽奥航运公司根本无法与这些身怀绝技的人抗衡。\n游走于犯罪生涯所练就的谨慎与迅捷，让她的团队占尽优势。\n她最终积攒下足够的财富买下了这家公司，从此独霸整个行业。

column5: Though Nada perished in Balteus, her end of the treaty was posthumously honored.\nA new nation was created, splitting Mazeo in half. A nation where pirates could live in freedom.\nTheir criminal records were expunged, and they began a new life, all thanks to Nada's efforts.
column6: 尽管娜达殒命于巴尔泰乌斯，但她那部分条约仍被追认履行。\n一个崭新的国家就此诞生，将马泽奥一分为二。那是一个海盗得以自由生活的国度。\n他们的犯罪记录被抹去，从此开启新的人生——这一切都要归功于娜达的努力。

column5: With their expertise and knowledge on secret routes, they quickly became the new masters.\nOverpowering The Mazean Shipping company, all trading was now under their watchful eyes.\nLifted trade bans and clean criminal records combined to help them dominate the industry.
column6: 凭着一身本领和对秘密航路的了解，他们很快成为新的霸主。\n他们压倒了马泽奥航运公司，所有贸易如今都在他们的监视之下。\n贸易禁令的解除与清白的档案，共同助他们称霸了整个行业。

column5: Alex didn't seem interested in this new pirate utopia, however.\nWith his criminal record erased, he started to enjoy life like everybody else.\nEventually offering to serve The New Monarchy's naval army, he became a general.
column6: 不过，亚历克斯似乎对这个新的海盗乌托邦毫无兴趣。\n犯罪记录被抹去后，他开始像其他人一样享受生活。\n最终，他主动请缨效力于新王权的海军，成为了一名将军。

column5: Shane was never seen again after that fateful encounter in Balteus.\nHe is presumed dead, and many refuse to speak about his betrayal.\nIf he survived, he went to great lengths to remain hidden from the world.
column6: 自巴尔泰乌斯那场命中注定的遭遇之后，肖恩便再未现身。\n人们推定他已死，许多人也不愿再提起他的背叛。\n如果他活了下来，那他必定费尽心机，隐匿于世。

column5: Shane was killed in action during the final assault on Balteus.\nMany members of The New Monarchy refused to speak about his betrayal.\nThe wounds he inflicted in your cause were grievous, and his justice was served.
column6: 肖恩在攻打巴尔泰乌斯的最后一场战斗中阵亡。\n新王权的许多成员都不愿再提起他的背叛。\n他给你们的事业造成的创伤极其沉重，而他已得到应有的审判。

column5: When the chaos and confusion settled down, Halin seemed like a new man.\nHe likened his existence to that of a spectator watching a performance.\nNo matter what he wanted to do, his body could not defy his Masters.
column6: 当混乱与困惑平息下来，哈林仿佛变成了另一个人。\n他将自己的存在比作一名观看表演的旁观者。\n无论他想做什么，他的身体都无法违抗他的主人们。

column5: He decided to atone for what he had done, and joined The New Monarchy.\nOf course, many people were apprehensive about accepting his aid.\nOver time, they learned to accept him and his desires as genuine.
column6: 他决定为自己所做的一切赎罪，并加入了新王权。\n当然，许多人都对接受他的帮助心存疑虑。\n随着时间推移，他们渐渐学会接受他，也相信他的心意是真诚的。

column5: His job stayed largely the same — ensuring that Alestia's rulers remained in power.\nBut with new masters, and even new friends, he took pride in being on the right side.
column6: 他的职责大体上没变——确保阿莱斯蒂亚的统治者们稳坐权位。\n但有了新的主人，甚至新的朋友，他为自己站在正确的一边而自豪。

column5: Halin fell during the final assault on Balteus — by your hands.\nWhen his true nature came to light, many wondered if you made the right choice.\nCould he have been liberated? And if so, could he ever be trusted? Nobody knew.
column6: 哈林在攻打巴尔泰乌斯的最后一场战斗中倒下——死于你手。\n当他的真实身份浮出水面，许多人开始怀疑你是否做对了选择。\n他本可以被解放吗？若能，他又是否值得信任？没人知道。

column5: But some would say that this was for the best, and the public moved on to believe it.\nWith a history of moles and defectors in this war — risks were too dangerous.\nDifficult choices needed to be made. You were all too familiar with that fact.
column6: 但有人会说这样对大家都好，民众也渐渐接受了这种说法。\n这场战争中向来不乏内奸与叛徒——风险实在太过危险。\n必须做出艰难的抉择。你对这个事实再清楚不过了。

column5: With the dark idol gone from Balteus, the corruption slowly waned.\nOver the next several decades, it made a complete transformation.\nMany would call it the most beautiful place in all of Alestian history.
column6: 黑暗灵像从巴尔泰乌斯消失后，腐化之力渐渐消退。\n在接下来的数十年里，它完成了彻底的蜕变。\n许多人称它为阿莱斯蒂亚历史上最美的地方。

column5: Its name was changed to \"New Balteus\", and left behind its old roots.\nNo longer would it be known as the seat of the tyrannical Triumvirate.\nPeople would see it as the place where Alestia was changed forever.
column6: 它被更名为“新巴尔泰乌斯”，彻底告别了它的旧日根基。\n它不再是那个暴虐的三人执政团盘踞之地。\n在人们心中，这里是阿莱斯蒂亚被彻底改变的地方。

column5: People would come from all over the world to see the home of The New Monarchy.\nIt became a symbol of new beginnings — teaching people that change is always possible.\nAs the corruption slowly disappeared, people settled down and turned it into a prosperous nation.
column6: 人们从世界各地前来，只为一睹新王权的家园。\n它成了新生的象征——教导人们，改变永远都是可能的。\n随着腐化渐渐褪去，人们在此安顿下来，将它变成了一片繁荣的国土。

column5: You were loved by all of your subjects, and led the world into a new age.\nBut guiding everybody to the bright future you secured would be a journey of its own.\nAnd knowing that fact made one thing clear — your work had only just begun.
column6: 你深受所有子民的爱戴，引领世界迈入了一个崭新的时代。\n但引导所有人走向你所开创的光明未来，本身也是一段漫长的旅程。\n明白这一点，有一件事便再清楚不过——你的工作才刚刚开始。

column5: You were successful in your aspirations. You left behind an entirely changed world.\nThe members of The Rebellion that survived had a new, even bigger journey before them.\nIt was time to lead the world into the bright future you secured. For them, work had only just begun.
column6: 你的抱负都已实现。你留下了一个彻底改变的世界。\n幸存下来的反抗军成员，面前还有一段更宏大、更艰巨的旅程。\n是时候引领世界走向你开创的光明未来了。对他们来说，工作才刚刚开始。

column5: Thank you for your service, Monarch.\nFor everything you've done, you will never be forgotten.
column6: 感谢你的付出，君主。\n你所做的一切，将永远被人铭记。

column5: I stumble down the stairs, making my way to the atrium.{w}\nHolding the destroyed Blade of Exodus, I use it for support.{w}\nIt would never jeopardize the future of other innocent worlds.
column6: 我踉跄着走下楼梯，朝中庭走去。{w}\n我握着已被毁去的流亡之刃，靠它支撑着身体。{w}\n它再也不会危及其他无辜世界的未来。

column5: But I start to wonder if I may have made the wrong decision.{w}\nI used the blade to temporarily destroy that idol. It wasn't gone for good.{w}\nWherever it ended up in the future, how would {i}they{/i} fight it off...?
column6: 但我开始怀疑，自己是不是做错了决定。{w}\n我用那把刃暂时摧毁了那尊灵像。它并未就此彻底消失。{w}\n无论它将来流落到哪里，{i}他们{/i}又该如何抵御它……？

column5: Or maybe, not having to rely on the Blade of Exodus was a good thing.{w}\nMaybe the next world it plagued could create another means to destroy it.{w}\nAll I knew for sure, was that the blade was destroyed, and Alestia was safe.
column6: 又或者，不必再依赖流亡之刃，反而是件好事。{w}\n也许它将要祸害的下一个世界，能创造别的办法来摧毁它。{w}\n我唯一确定的是，刃已毁去，而阿莱斯蒂亚安全了。

column5: As I move, I see flashes. Almost like I'm having visions.{w}\nI know I couldn't see the future, but for a moment, it felt like I did.{w}\nI can't explain it, but it felt like I knew what became of our lives.
column6: 我一边前行，一边看到闪烁的画面。几乎像是在看见幻象。{w}\n我知道自己无法预见未来，但那一刻，感觉就像真的看见了。{w}\n我无法解释，但我感觉自己知道我们的人生后来变成了什么样。

column5: At least, those that survived.{w}\nIf it {i}was{/i} a vision, then I take it as one final gift.
column6: 至少，是那些活下来的人。{w}\n如果这{i}真的{/i}是幻象，那我就把它当作最后的礼物。

column5: When I arrive back at the entrance, I see exactly who I expected.{w}\nJust as we had planned, everybody made their way here after the battle.{w}\nIt takes a few seconds before they notice me, but they all quickly approach me.
column6: 当我回到入口时，看到的人正是我所预料的那些。{w}\n正如我们事先计划的那样，战后所有人都来到了这里。{w}\n过了几秒他们才发现我，但很快就都围了上来。

column5: [firstname]! I'm so glad you made it.\nWhen the castle started shaking, I feared for the worst.\nI'm just glad I got to ring that bell. I saved {i}so{/i} many lives!
column6: [firstname]！我真高兴你平安回来了。\n城堡开始摇晃的时候，我还以为最坏的情况要发生了。\n我真庆幸自己敲响了那口钟。我救了{i}那么{/i}多条命！

column5: I'll admit, I was starting to worry as well.\nSorry if you were scared when we parted ways earlier.\nBut thanks to those daggers, they didn't stand a chance.
column6: 我承认，我也开始担心了。\n之前我们分开的时候，要是让你害怕了，我很抱歉。\n但多亏了那些匕首，他们根本不堪一击。

column5: I'm not gonna lie, I was almost dead meat.\nIf it weren't for Gryz, I would've been a goner for sure.\nAnd here I thought that I preferred sneaking alone. Heh.
column6: 不骗你，我差点就没命了。\n要不是格瑞兹，我肯定就完蛋了。\n我还一直以为自己更喜欢独自潜行呢。呵。

column5: I'm glad that you saw it through to the end, [firstname].\nSomething told me that helping you was the right thing to do.\nAfter today, I can rest easy knowing that I made the right choice.
column6: 我很高兴你坚持到了最后，[firstname]。\n我总觉得，帮你是个正确的决定。\n过了今天，我就能安心地知道自己选对了。

column5: Then, I see Ulric approach me from the other side.{w}\nIt was good to see him alive. I can tell that he's super happy.{w}\nAll the stress and worry seemed to melt away from the room when I arrived.
column6: 这时，我看见乌尔里克从另一边朝我走来。{w}\n看到他还活着真好。看得出他特别开心。{w}\n我一到场，房间里所有的紧张与担忧仿佛都烟消云散了。

column5: Everything went as planned?\nI bet you have some pretty interesting stories to tell.\nSave it for later though, there's a lot of work to do.
column6: 一切按计划进行吗？\n我敢打赌，你肯定有不少有趣的故事要讲。\n不过还是留到以后吧，我们还有很多事要做。

column5: Seeing you again is certainly a welcome surprise, [firstname].\nYou hold the honor of being the one who took down The Triumvirate.\nWear that badge with pride. You've guided the world to a perfect future.
column6: 能再次见到你，真是个意外的惊喜，[firstname]。\n你肩负着扳倒三人执政团的那份荣耀。\n带着这份勋章骄傲地活下去吧。你引领世界走向了完美的未来。

column5: You'll never guess what happened, [firstname]!\nJust as I was about to fall in battle, Shane came to my rescue.\nI'm not sure where he is now, but I've sent out a search party.
column6: 你绝对猜不到发生了什么，[firstname]！\n就在我快要战死的时候，肖恩赶来救了我。\n我不知道他现在在哪，但我已经派出搜救队了。

column5: Everybody gathers around me, looking at the broken blade.{w}\nI guess there was no point in holding onto it anymore.{w}\nI throw it to the ground. I'd never use it again.
column6: 众人围拢到我身边，注视着那把断裂的刃。{w}\n我想，再留着它也没什么意义了。{w}\n我把它扔在地上。我永远不会再用它。

column5: But I consider it a blessing that I'd never {i}need{/i} to.{w}\nI survived, and The Blade of Exodus was no more.
column6: 但我庆幸自己永远不必{i}需要{/i}它。{w}\n我活了下来，而流亡之刃已不复存在。

column5: Nobody would ever again be tempted and seduced by its power.{w}\nI did my part, and for that, it was time that I got some rest.
column6: 再也不会有人被它的力量所诱惑、所蛊惑。{w}\n我已尽了自己的本分，现在，是时候歇一歇了。

column5: Wait. Rest...?\nYou know there won't be any time for that, right?\nYou're the ruler of this world, now. There's still so much left to do.
column6: 等等。歇一歇……？\n你知道根本没时间让你歇吧？\n你现在是这个世界的主宰。还有太多事要做。

column5: He's right. Taking down The Triumvirate was just the first step.\nWe need to tell the people what happened, and earn their loyalty.
column6: 他说得对。扳倒三人执政团只是第一步。\n我们得告诉民众发生了什么，并赢得他们的忠诚。

column5: But it won't be all bad, right...?\nI mean, we'll have your back the entire time.
column6: 但也不会全是坏事，对吧……？\n我是说，我们会一直支持你的。

column5: I let out a soft laugh, but then stumble over.{w}\nFortaime and Ulric grab onto me, and support me.{w}\nI guess I wasn't holding up as well as I thought.
column6: 我轻笑了一声，却忽然踉跄了一下。{w}\n福泰姆和乌尔里克扶住我，把我撑了起来。{w}\n看来我并没有自己以为的那样撑得住。

column5: Whoa – watch your step, [firstname].\nHere, let's find you a place to sit down.
column6: 哇——当心脚下，[firstname]。\n来，我们给你找个地方坐下。

column5: Yeah, then we can talk about what happens next.\nRemember, this isn't the end. It's just the beginning.
column6: 对，然后我们再商量接下来怎么办。\n记住，这不是结束。这只是开始。

column5: I smile, as I remain in the arms of my comrades.{w}\nThey didn't know what happened next, but I still felt like I did.{w}\nAnd Fortaime was right. It was a new beginning – for every Alestian.
column6: 我微笑着，依偎在同伴们的臂弯里。{w}\n他们不知道接下来会发生什么，但我依然觉得自己知道。{w}\n福泰姆说得对。这是一个新的开始——属于每一个阿莱斯蒂亚人。

column5: My vision fades in, and I feel incredibly confused.{w}\nWith everything that just happened, I should definitely be dead.{w}\nActually, maybe I was. Far be it from me to decide what death brought.
column6: 我的视线渐渐清晰，心中满是困惑。{w}\n经历了刚刚的一切，我按理说肯定已经死了。{w}\n其实，也许我确实死了。死亡带来什么，也轮不到我来断定。

column5: I know that I'm in my house. That much is easily discernible.{w}\nAfter rising up to a sitting position, though, I notice something shocking.{w}\nThe lower half of my arm is still missing. Could I have survived...?
column6: 我认得出来自己在家里。这一点很容易分辨。{w}\n可当我撑起身子坐起来后，却注意到一件令人震惊的事。{w}\n我手臂的下半截依然不见踪影。难道我活下来了……？

column5: No. That was impossible. So what's going on, exactly...?{w}\nAs my mind starts to fill with possibilities, there's a knock at my door.{w}\nI'm filled with fright. But then, a moment later, I hear a familiar voice.
column6: 不。那不可能。那到底是怎么回事……？{w}\n当各种猜测开始在我脑中涌现，门外传来了敲门声。{w}\n我满是恐惧。但片刻之后，我听到了一个熟悉的声音。

column5: Hey – open up!
column6: 嘿——开门！

column5: I rush to the door, and Fortaime steps inside of my house.{w}\nMy heart is beating so fast. Then, joy overtakes me.{w}\nI give Fortaime a big hug, and he seems surprised.
column6: 我冲向门口，福泰姆走进了我的家。{w}\n我的心跳得飞快。紧接着，喜悦淹没了我。{w}\n我给了福泰姆一个大大的拥抱，他看上去有些惊讶。

column5: Did you just wake up...!?\nOh jeeze, I hope we won't be late.\nDon't tell me you forgot what day it is!
column6: 你才刚醒吗……！？\n哦天哪，希望我们不会迟到。\n别告诉我你忘了今天是什么日子！

column5: Huh...?
It's the anniversary of your induction!\nIf we don't hurry to the Town Square, we'll be late.\nSalus is already under {i}enough{/i} stress, having to train Mylus.
column6: 是你受封的周年纪念日！\n要是我们不快点赶到城镇广场，就要迟到了。\n萨卢斯光是训练迈勒斯，就已经够{i}头疼{/i}了。

column5: Salus is alive...?
column6: 萨卢斯还活着……？

column5: So come on, we need to get going.\nYour parents are counting on me, [firstname].\nI told them to give me ten minutes, tops!
column6: 所以快走吧，我们得出发了。\n你父母都指望我呢，[firstname]。\n我跟他们说了，最多给我十分钟！

column5: So come on, we need to get going.\nYour parents are counting on me, [firstname].\nI told them to give me ten minutes, tops!
column6: 所以快走吧，我们得出发了。\n你父母都指望我呢，[firstname]。\n我跟他们说了，最多给我十分钟！

column5: My... parents...?{w}\nI'm in complete shock, and I stand there, dumbfounded.{w}\nA small eternity passes, before Fortaime breaks the silence.
column6: 我……的父母……？{w}\n我完全惊呆了，呆呆地站在原地。{w}\n仿佛过了漫长的一瞬，福泰姆才打破沉默。

column5: Well don't just stand there! You need to get ready!\nAt this rate, you'll be greeting the townspeople in your underwear.\nI mean, you can if you want to. But I {i}really{/i} don't recommend that.
column6: 别光站在那儿啊！你得去准备一下！\n再这样下去，你就要穿着内衣去迎接镇上的居民了。\n我是说，你想那样也行。但我{i}真的{/i}不建议。

column5: I don't know what's going on. Am I in a new reality...?{w}\nThe Elder is alive, as well as my parents; {i}and{/i} I've been inducted?{w}\nThis means that The Rebellion was never formed. There was no occupation.
column6: 我不知道发生了什么。我是不是身处一个新的现实……？{w}\n长老还活着，我的父母也是；{i}而且{/i}我还受了封？{w}\n这意味着反抗军从未成立。也从未有过占领。

column5: Tears start streaming from my eyes, and I give Fortaime a bigger hug.{w}\nI don't know what happened, exactly, but I'm not about to question it.{w}\nIf this was the reward for my journey, and sacrifice, then it was worth it.
column6: 泪水开始从我眼中涌出，我给了福泰姆一个更紧的拥抱。{w}\n我搞不清到底发生了什么，但我不打算去质疑它。{w}\n如果这是我一路旅程与牺牲换来的回报，那就值得。

column5: Whoa – hey! Calm down.
column6: 哇——嘿！冷静点。

column5: I cry even harder, and Fortaime can't help but show worry.
column6: 我哭得更厉害了，福泰姆忍不住露出担忧的神色。

column5: Hey, wait, are you okay...?
column6: 嘿，等等，你还好吗……？

column5: I nod, and tell him that everything is fine.{w}\nAnd this time, something tells me it will stay that way.
column6: 我点点头，告诉他一切都好。{w}\n而这一次，我有种预感，一切都会一直好下去。

column5: I invite Valessa into my room, since she seems unable to get to sleep.{w}\nThat seems to be the case with almost everybody. We were too worried to sleep.{w}\nShe scans the room, taking in all the sights. It really was an impressive place to behold.
column6: 我邀请瓦莱莎进我的房间，因为她似乎怎么也睡不着。{w}\n几乎所有人都这样。我们太过担忧，难以入眠。{w}\n她环视房间，把每一处都看了个遍。这里确实是个令人叹为观止的地方。

column5: This room is pretty cool, [firstname].\nIt makes sense that you'd get it, too.\nMust feel good, being royalty and all.
column6: 这房间挺酷的，[firstname]。\n你会分到它也是理所当然。\n当王室成员的感觉一定不错吧。

column5: I'm pretty confident after hearing Damek's plan.\nI get to follow you to the castle too, so that makes me happy.\nYou can trust me to have your back if anything bad happens.
column6: 听完达梅克的计划，我相当有信心。\n我还能跟着你一起进城堡，这让我很开心。\n要是出了什么坏事，你尽管放心，有我在你身后。

column5: Let's hope it doesn't come to that.
column6: 但愿不会到那一步。

column5: I've been practicing with those daggers I got from Mazeo, actually.\nThey took some getting used to, but I think I can hold my own.\nNot that those suits of armor require much to take down.
column6: 其实我一直在拿从马泽奥弄来的那些匕首练习。\n用起来花了我些时间才习惯，但我觉得我能应付。\n倒不是说那些铠甲有多难对付。

column5: It's true. They were pretty weak.{w}\nThe Triumvirate focused on quantity, not quality.{w}\nHopefully that would be their downfall as we proceeded.
column6: 没错。它们确实很弱。{w}\n三人执政团注重的是数量，而非质量。{w}\n但愿随着我们推进，这会是他们的致命弱点。

column5: To be honest, I'm really scared that we might not survive.\nI mean, victory usually comes at a cost. But what will we pay...?\nIf I make it out of this without my friends, I'll just feel so hollow.
column6: 老实说，我真的很怕我们可能活不下来。\n我是说，胜利通常都要付出代价。可我们要付出什么呢……？\n如果活下来的我却失去了朋友们，那我只会觉得空落落的。

column5: Especially since I'm expected to lead Valinorth after all of this is over.\nWithout you and Fortaime, I'd just feel so lost in this world.\nYou give me strength; and I'll be needing that strength.
column6: 尤其是等这一切结束后，我还得去领导瓦利诺斯。\n没有你和福泰姆，我只会觉得在这世上迷失了方向。\n你给我力量；而我正需要这份力量。

column5: I tell her that I'm not planning on going anywhere.{w}\nWhatever comes next, we'd handle it as a team.{w}\nWe didn't come this far just to perish in the end.
column6: 我告诉她，我没打算去任何地方。{w}\n无论接下来发生什么，我们都会作为一个团队去面对。{w}\n我们走了这么远，不是为了在最后殒命。

column5: I want to help fix Mazeo, but I don't want to do it alone.\nIt's up to us to help undo the damage inflicted by our parents.\nWith you in the throne, I think we could do it pretty easily.
column6: 我想帮忙修复马泽奥，但我不想独自去做。\n弥补我们父辈造成的伤害，是我们义不容辞的责任。\n有你在王座上，我想我们能轻轻松松做到。

column5: She seems really fixated on helping Mazeo. Almost obligated, even.{w}\nIt makes sense, since she feels that our families are responsible for a lot.{w}\nWhen I took the throne, I'm sure I'd be able to help her out. It's a good cause.
column6: 她似乎一心想着帮助马泽奥。甚至像是觉得责无旁贷。{w}\n这说得通，因为在她看来，我们的家族要负很大责任。{w}\n等我登上王座，我一定能帮她一把。这是件好事。

column5: I really need to stop thinking so far ahead.\nThis is the eve of our final battle. I should focus on that.\nGetting lost in thought on the battlefield would be the death of me.
column6: 我真的不能再想得那么远了。\n这是我们决战的前夜。我该把心思放在眼前。\n在战场上走神，会要了我的命。

column5: So let's just enjoy this moment, shall we?\nThis might be the last time we're able to hang out.\nI'd hate to tarnish it by freaking out and acting stupid.
column6: 所以，我们就好好享受此刻，好吗？\n这也许是我们最后一次能这样相处了。\n我可不想因为自己抓狂犯傻，把这一刻毁了。

column5: I tell her that it's fine — I enjoy her company regardless.{w}\nBesides, I'm sharing a lot of the same worry. We're in this together.{w}\nWhen we met up to launch the attack, we'd have no idea what came next.
column6: 我告诉她没关系——无论如何，我都很享受有她相伴。{w}\n况且，我也怀着一模一样的担忧。我们同在一条船上。{w}\n等我们集结发起进攻时，谁也不知道接下来会发生什么。

column5: Well, at least I don't feel so alone anymore.\nFortaime is always so carefree, no matter what happens.\nTalking to him, you'd never guess that we could all die here.
column6: 至少我不再觉得那么孤单了。\n福泰姆无论发生什么，总是那么漫不经心。\n和他聊天，你根本想不到我们都可能死在这里。

column5: Before I stop being so gloomy, can you promise me one thing?\nIt'll make me feel a lot better — and morale is what we need right now.
column6: 在我停止这么消沉之前，你能答应我一件事吗？\n这会让我的心情好很多——而此刻我们正需要士气。

column5: I nod — but it's really dependent on what the favor entails.
column6: 我点点头——但这其实取决于她要求的是什么。

column5: If I do end up dying out there, I just want Valinorth to be okay.\nCan you promise me that you'll find a capable Elder to replace me?\nThey don't have to share my views. I just want our home to prosper.
column6: 如果我真的死在外面，我只希望瓦利诺斯安然无恙。\n你能答应我，会找一位能干的继任者来接替我当长老吗？\n对方不必和我见解一致。我只希望我们的家园能够兴旺。

column5: I nod. That's definitely something I could do for her.{w}\nThat is — if I survived. But I don't display such doubt right now.{w}\nIt's best that I try to look strong and resolute for all of my allies.
column6: 我点点头。这绝对是我能为她做的事。{w}\n前提是——我能活下来。但此刻我不能流露出这种疑虑。{w}\n对所有盟友，我最好都表现出坚强与坚定。

column5: If I do end up dying out there, can you help repair Mazeo?\nI just want to see a happy nation. It's gone through so much.\nOur parents hurt it — so we should be the ones who mend it.
column6: 如果我真的死在外面，你能帮忙修复马泽奥吗？\n我只想看到一个幸福的国度。它已经承受了太多。\n我们的父辈伤害了它——所以我们该是抚平它的人。

column5: I nod. That's definitely something I could do for her.{w}\nThat is — if I survived. But I don't display such doubt right now.{w}\nIt's best that I try to look strong and resolute for all of my allies.
column6: 我点点头。这绝对是我能为她做的事。{w}\n前提是——我能活下来。但此刻我不能流露出这种疑虑。{w}\n对所有盟友，我最好都表现出坚强与坚定。

column5: Good. Then we can move on to better things.\nYou know, I've been thinking about how far we've come.\nI've seen so much, and I feel like a totally different person.
column6: 那就好。这样我们就能继续做更重要的事了。\n你知道吗，我一直在想我们走了多远。\n我见识了太多，觉得自己已经彻底变了个人。

column5: I wonder what would've happened if things were different.\nWhat if your induction ceremony wasn't cancelled? \nWhat if you never got that deceiving vision...?
column6: 我在想，如果一切不同，会是什么样子。\n如果你的受封仪式没有被取消呢？\n如果你从未看到那个骗人的幻象呢……？

column5: She steps forward and places her hands in mine.
column6: 她上前一步，把双手放进我的掌心。

column5: Would we still be as close as we are right now?\nYou know, that moment we shared in Mazeo was so special.\nGiven time — I want this bond to grow even stronger. Do you?
column6: 我们还会像现在这样亲密吗？\n你知道吗，我们在马泽奥共度的那段时光，是那么特别。\n假以时日——我希望这份羁绊能变得更加深厚。你呢？

column5: I nod. I made the choice to pursue this relationship, after all.{w}\nBut she's right. We might not be this close if not for all the hardships.{w}\nAt least it's proof that even in war, beautiful things can still happen.
column6: 我点点头。毕竟，是我选择了去追求这段感情。{w}\n但她说得对。若不是经历了那些磨难，我们或许不会这般亲密。{w}\n至少这证明了，即便在战争中，美好的事依然可能发生。

column5: I don't want to rush this and do something stupid.\nPart of me wants to, given the circumstances — but we shouldn't.\nLet's just make a vow. We'll both survive, and take things slow.
column6: 我不想操之过急，做出什么蠢事。\n在这样的处境下，我有一半的心思很想——但我们不该那样。\n我们就立个誓吧。我们都要活下来，然后慢慢来。

column5: With a smile, she squeezes my hands, and I do so in return.{w}\nTaking a step forward, she places a soft kiss on my cheek.{w}\nI smile back, and wrap my arms around her as tight as I can.
column6: 她微笑着捏了捏我的手，我也回握了她。{w}\n她上前一步，在我脸颊上轻轻落下一吻。{w}\n我笑着回应，尽我所能地紧紧抱住她。

column5: I really hope we make it through this...
column6: 我真心希望我们能挺过这一关……

column5: I try not to get sad, but my eyes tear up ever so slightly.{w}\nHugging her tighter, I rub my hands up and down her back.{w}\nWe've come too far to lose each other. That's what I tell her.
column6: 我努力不让自己难过，眼眶却还是微微泛红。{w}\n我把她抱得更紧，双手在她背上来回轻抚。{w}\n我们走到今天不容易，绝不能失去彼此。我就是这么告诉她。

column5: Thank you...
column6: 谢谢你……

column5: A few moments later, we break the hug.{w}\nBut when I do, I feel closer than we ever have before.
column6: 片刻之后，我们松开了拥抱。{w}\n但松开的那一刻，我却觉得我们比以往任何时候都更亲近。

column5: Who would we be — if not for all that's happened so far?\nI mean, we were simple residents of Valinorth just a while back.\nBut now, we stand in Balteus, ready to fight the rulers of the world.
column6: 若不是经历了迄今为止的一切，我们会是什么样的人？\n我是说，不久前我们还只是瓦利诺斯普通的居民。\n可如今，我们站在巴尔泰乌斯，准备对抗这个世界的统治者。

column5: I wouldn't believe it if I didn't see it unfold right in front of me.\nBut you know, I'm not sure which version of myself I'd rather be.\nIt's not an easy thing — knowing how twisted the world truly is.
column6: 若不是亲眼看着它在我眼前展开，我绝不会相信。\n但你知道吗，我也说不清自己更愿意做哪一个版本的我。\n得知这个世界究竟有多扭曲——这并不容易接受。

column5: That's a tough call. I don't know which version of myself I'd rather be, either.{w}\nIt makes me think back on where I started, and where I am right now.{w}\nPutting the whole journey into perspective, I realize how I've changed.
column6: 这确实很难说。我也说不清自己更愿意做哪一个版本的我。{w}\n这让我回想起自己从哪里出发，又身处何方。{w}\n把整个旅程放在一起看，我才意识到自己改变了多少。

column5: Obviously we can't go back and change anything...\nBut it's just weird to think about; and it was all out of our control.\nLet's hope that after this, we can take things in the direction {i}we{/i} want.
column6: 显然我们无法回到过去改变什么……\n但光是想想就很奇怪；而且这一切都不在我们的掌控之中。\n但愿经历了这些之后，我们能朝着{i}自己{/i}想要的方向前进。

column5: The people will be free to live as they please.\nThey'll never have to lose their homes, or comply with tyrants.\nIf that's the end goal here — then I'd say our changing was worth it.
column6: 人们将自由地按自己的意愿生活。\n他们再也不必失去家园，或屈从于暴君。\n如果这就是最终的目标——那我会说，我们的改变是值得的。

column5: Thinking of it that way, I agree. I'm just glad we haven't changed {i}too{/i} much.{w}\nWith how grey things can get during war — some people commit atrocities.{w}\nI'd to my best to be a just ruler, even if I wouldn't be able to please everybody.
column6: 这么一想，我表示同意。我只是庆幸我们还没有变得{i}太过{/i}不同。{w}\n考虑到战争中事情会变得多么黑白难辨——有些人会犯下暴行。{w}\n我会尽力做一个公正的统治者，即便我无法让所有人都满意。

column5: Thank you so much for inviting me over, [firstname].\nI feel a lot better than I did just a few minutes ago.\nI guess I'll see you when we gather to launch the attack?
column6: 非常感谢你邀请我过来，[firstname]。\n我感觉比几分钟前好多了。\n那我们集合发起进攻的时候再见？

column5: I nod. That time was fast approaching.{w}\nI see her out of the room, and let out a huge sigh.{w}\nTalking to my friends — for maybe the last time? It's crushing me.
column6: 我点点头。那个时刻正迅速逼近。{w}\n我送她出了房间，长长地叹了口气。{w}\n和朋友们交谈——也许是最后一次？这让我心碎。

column5: But if I didn't, and they perished — I'd regret it forever.{w}\nThat's the excuse I give myself for enduring this pain.{w}\nTurning to face the big open room, I wonder what's next.
column6: 但如果我不这么做，而他们却死了——我会后悔一辈子。{w}\n这就是我用来忍受这份痛苦的理由。{w}\n转身面对这间空旷的大屋，我不知道接下来会怎样。

column5: A knock sounds at my door, and I open it without hesitation.{w}\nFortaime is there. He looks a bit upset, so I invite him inside.{w}\nLooking around the room, he lets out a loud and anxious sigh.
column6: 门外传来敲门声，我毫不犹豫地打开了门。{w}\n福泰姆站在那里。他看上去有些不安，我便请他进来。{w}\n他环顾房间，发出了一声响亮而焦虑的叹息。

column5: I'm gonna be honest, [firstname].\nI'm scared. Terrified. I don't know what's gonna happen.\nI mean, climbing The Triumvirate's castle? That's insane.
column6: 老实跟你说，[firstname]。\n我害怕。我怕得要命。我不知道会发生什么。\n我是说，去爬三人执政团的城堡？那简直疯了。

column5: Not to mention that the entire battle hinges on my success.\nI have those metallic claws, but I don't know how much that'll help.\nTheir castle is probably made of stone — like this library is.
column6: 更别说整场战斗都取决于我的成败。\n我有那些金属爪，但我不知道能有多大用。\n他们的城堡多半是石头砌的——就像这座图书馆一样。

column5: He starts pacing around the room, with extreme worry.
column6: 他开始在房间里踱来踱去，满脸极度的忧虑。

column5: What if I fall? What if I get shot by an arrow?\nIf anything gets in the way, I might not be able to do this.\nI require extreme focus, you know. This is too much.
column6: 要是我掉下去怎么办？要是我中箭怎么办？\n只要有任何东西挡道，我可能就做不到了。\n要知道，我需要极度专注。这太难了。

column5: I can imagine that climbing during a battle is hard.{w}\nNormally, the only danger he'd have to worry about is falling off.{w}\nBut during this, he'd be a huge target for any archers nearby.
column6: 我能想象，在战斗中攀爬有多难。{w}\n平时他唯一要担心的危险，就是从上面摔下来。{w}\n可在这场战斗里，他会成为附近任何弓箭手的巨大靶子。

column5: Sorry to come here and panic like this.\nIt {i}could{/i} end up being our last night together, after all.\nThere are probably way better ways to spend it than this.
column6: 抱歉跑来跟你这样惊慌失措。\n毕竟，这{i}可能{/i}会是我们共度的最后一晚。\n本该有远比这更好的方式来度过。

column5: He stops pacing around, and stops right in front of me.{w}\nTaking slow breaths, I can tell he's trying to calm down.{w}\nI let him have his time, and he's back to normal pretty fast.
column6: 他停下踱步，正好停在我面前。{w}\n缓缓地呼吸着，我看得出他在努力平静下来。{w}\n我任由他自己调整，他很快就恢复了常态。

column5: Okay Fortaime, you got this.\nYou're gonna climb the tower, and ring the bell of retreat.\nYou'll help win the battle, and return to Valinorth as a hero.
column6: 好了福泰姆，你能行的。\n你要爬上那座塔，敲响撤退的钟。\n你会帮我们打赢这场仗，然后作为英雄回到瓦利诺斯。

column5: Trust me, I never forgot that you appointed me as The Elder.\nI'll do my best to lead Valinorth in the right direction, I promise.\nBut if I don't make it, you'll have to find someone else to lead.
column6: 相信我，我从未忘记是你任命我为长老的。\n我保证，会尽力引领瓦利诺斯走上正确的方向。\n但如果我没能活下来，你就得另找一个人来领导了。

column5: I know you're gonna tell me not to worry.\nI know you're going to say that everything will be fine.\nBut that's not true. We all need to be realistic here.
column6: 我知道你会叫我别担心。\n我知道你会说一切都会好起来。\n但那不是真的。我们在这里都得现实一点。

column5: You know, I've been thinking about what I should do after the war.\nAnd I think I want to move to Mazeo. I want to help the nation reform.\nIt's been hurt so much, even by our parents. It deserves happiness.
column6: 你知道吗，我一直在想战后该做什么。\n我想我可能会搬去马泽奥。我想帮那个国家重整旗鼓。\n它受的伤太重了，连我们的父辈都伤害过它。它理应得到幸福。

column5: Valessa has her calling as the next Elder of Valinorth.\nI'd be your Scribe, if visions weren't becoming a thing of the past.\nAt the end of the day, it seems like the smartest choice for me to make.
column6: 瓦莱莎有自己的使命，要做瓦利诺斯的下一任长老。\n如果预言不再有用，我本可以做你的书记官。\n说到底，这似乎是我能做出的最明智的选择。

column5: That is, if I don't die during the battle tomorrow.\nI know what you're going to say. \"Don't worry — you'll be fine.\"\nI wish that were true, but it's not. We need to be realistic here.
column6: 前提是，我明天不会战死。\n我知道你要说什么。“别担心——你会没事的。”\n我也希望那是真的，可它不是。我们得现实一点。

column5: There's a chance that we could lose this war tomorrow.\nThere's a chance that all of us could die. A really big chance.\nWe're not immortal. We need to face the facts, not live in denial.
column6: 我们明天有可能输掉这场战争。\n我们所有人都有可能死去。而且可能性很大。\n我们并非不死之身。得直面事实，而不是活在否认之中。

column5: They're all out there in the atrium with so much confidence.\nBut I know that deep down inside, they're scared too.\nWe all have something we're afraid of, you know?
column6: 他们都在中庭里，个个信心满满。\n但我知道，他们内心深处也同样害怕。\n我们都有害怕的东西，你知道吗？

column5: He steps forward and wraps his arms around me.{w}\nI can feel him tremble. I return the hug with a tight squeeze.
column6: 他上前一步，张开双臂抱住了我。{w}\n我能感觉到他在发抖。我紧紧地回抱了他。

column5: You know — it's not death that scares me, [firstname].\nIt's the thought of never seeing you again that pains my heart.\nI don't want to lose you. I've never been so scared in my life.
column6: 你知道吗——让我害怕的不是死亡，[firstname]。\n而是想到再也见不到你，才让我心痛。\n我不想失去你。我这一生从没这么害怕过。

column5: I tell him that I'm not planning on going anywhere.{w}\nAfter the war, we can settle down together, and be happy.
column6: 我告诉他，我没打算去任何地方。{w}\n战争结束后，我们可以一起安顿下来，幸福地生活。

column5: You can't be certain of that, though...\nJust like I can't be certain that {i}I'll{/i} survive.\nAll we can do is try — and hope for the best.
column6: 可你没法确定这一点……\n就像我也无法确定{i}自己{/i}一定能活下来。\n我们能做的只是尽力而为——然后祈求最好的结果。

column5: So promise me {i}one{/i} thing. No heroics, okay?\nNo grand acts of sacrifice. No trading your life.\nThis world needs you after the war. {i}I{/i} need you.
column6: 所以答应我{i}一件{/i}事。别逞英雄，好吗？\n不要什么壮烈的牺牲。不要拿自己的命去换。\n战后这个世界需要你。{i}我{/i}需要你。

column5: He starts shaking less, and we break the hug.{w}\nBut I agree, and tell him I'll try my best to comply.
column6: 他的颤抖渐渐平息，我们松开了拥抱。{w}\n但我答应了，并告诉他我会尽力做到。

column5: The thought of a world without you is almost too much to bear.\nI love you. I'll {i}always{/i} love you. I just hope we get a happy ending.\nAfter all we've been through, I think we deserve it — don't you?
column6: 一想到没有你的世界，我几乎就无法承受。\n我爱你。我会{i}永远{/i}爱你。我只希望我们能有幸福的结局。\n经历了这一切之后，我觉得我们值得拥有——你不觉得吗？

column5: I nod, and tell him that I love him too.{w}\nA smile appears on his face, and he immediately calms down.{w}\nI don't want to lose him either — I'm filled with all of the same frights.
column6: 我点点头，告诉他我也爱他。{w}\n他脸上露出笑容，立刻平静了下来。{w}\n我也不想失去他——我满心都是同样的恐惧。

column5: He steps forward and gives me a quick hug.{w}\nReturning it, I squeeze him before the hug is broken.
column6: 他上前一步，飞快地抱了我一下。{w}\n我回抱过去，在松开前用力搂了搂他。

column5: You know — it's not death that scares me, [firstname].\nIt's the thought of never seeing my friends again that hurts me.\nI don't want to lose anybody. I've never been this scared in my life.
column6: 你知道吗——让我害怕的不是死亡，[firstname]。\n而是想到再也见不到我的朋友们，才让我心痛。\n我不想失去任何人。我这一生从没这么害怕过。

column5: I tell him that I'm not planning on going anywhere.{w}\nAfter the war, we'll all be together, living peacefully.
column6: 我告诉他，我没打算去任何地方。{w}\n战争结束后，我们会全都在一起，平静地生活。

column5: You can't be certain of that, though.\nJust like I can't be certain that {i}I'll{/i} survive.\nAll we can do is try — and hope for the best.
column6: 可你没法确定这一点。\n就像我也无法确定{i}自己{/i}一定能活下来。\n我们能做的只是尽力而为——然后祈求最好的结果。

column5: So promise me {i}one{/i} thing. No heroics, okay?\nNo grand acts of sacrifice. No trading your life.\nThis world needs you after the war. We all need you.
column6: 所以答应我{i}一件{/i}事。别逞英雄，好吗？\n不要什么壮烈的牺牲。不要拿自己的命去换。\n战后这个世界需要你。我们都需要你。

column5: I agree, and tell him that I'll try my best to comply.{w}\nWe're almost at the end. It feels surreal to me.
column6: 我答应了，并告诉他我会尽力做到。{w}\n我们快到终点了。这一切让我觉得恍如梦境。

column5: I guess we'll find all of this out in a few hours anyway, right?\nIt's almost sunrise, and the battle shouldn't be too long.\nLet's change the subject. I've worried enough.
column6: 反正再过几个小时，我们就会知道这一切的结果了，对吧？\n天快亮了，这场仗应该不会打太久。\n换个话题吧。我已经担心够了。

column5: He strikes a thinking pose, and remains silent for a few moments.
column6: 他摆出一副冥思的姿态，沉默了好一会儿。

column5: Oh, here we go! If we win, we'll have a huge party.\nA party that the world will talk about forever!\nWe can give everybody Mazean apples!
column6: 哦，有了！要是我们赢了，就办一场盛大的派对。\n一场全世界都会永远传颂的派对！\n我们可以给所有人发马泽奥苹果！

column5: I smile — being happy that he's happy.{w}\nI tell him that we will have the biggest party the world has ever seen.{w}\nAnd if we try our best, and work together, we'll win this battle with ease.
column6: 我笑了——为他开心而开心。{w}\n我告诉他，我们会办一场全世界前所未见的盛大派对。{w}\n只要我们竭尽全力、齐心协力，就能轻松赢下这场战斗。

column5: Sweet! Then I can't wait!\nI'll let you get back to what you were doing, [firstname].\nThis isn't goodbye, after all. We'll be seeing each other again for sure.
column6: 太好了！那我可等不及了！\n我就不打扰你忙你的事了，[firstname]。\n毕竟这又不是永别。我们肯定还会再见面的。

column5: He leaves my room with a smile. A direct counterpoint to how he entered.{w}\nThat brings me a sense of ease. We needed to have a clear head right now.{w}\nIt's almost time for the attack. I should make wise use of the time I have left.
column6: 他带着笑容离开了我的房间。和他进来时的神情截然相反。{w}\n这让我感到一丝宽慰。此刻我们需要保持清醒的头脑。{w}\n进攻的时刻快到了。我该好好利用剩下的时间。

column5: I invite Pro over to my room to spend some final time together.{w}\nHe has the dangerous task of infiltrating The Triumvirate's castle.{w}\nThere's no telling what would happen, and I can tell that he's scared.
column6: 我邀请普洛来我的房间，共度最后一段时光。{w}\n他肩负着潜入三人执政团城堡的危险任务。{w}\n谁也不知道会发生什么，我看得出他很害怕。

column5: So, I guess this is it, huh...?\nYou know, I always thought that I'd be ready.\nBut now that we're here, I feel such apprehension.
column6: 那么，我猜就是现在了，是吧……？\n你知道吗，我一直以为自己会做好准备。\n可如今真到了这一步，我却感到如此忐忑。

column5: I know the layout of their castle based on past reconnaissance. \nBut when we stole The Blade of Exodus, they weren't expecting us.\nThey know we're here, now. For us, this will be a purely uphill battle.
column6: 根据过去的侦察，我了解他们城堡的布局。\n可当初我们偷走流亡之刃时，他们毫无防备。\n现在他们知道我们来了。对我们来说，这将是场纯粹的硬仗。

column5: He's right. We could no longer use the element of surprise.{w}\nWe had our strength, and our smarts. But would it be enough?
column6: 他说得对。我们再也无法利用奇袭的优势了。{w}\n我们有力量，也有智慧。但这够吗？

column5: Look at me, freaking out. I don't mean to bring down your morale.\nLet's change the subject, alright? Is there any wine in this place?
column6: 看看我，慌成这样。我不是有意打击你的士气。\n换个话题吧，好吗？这地方有酒吗？

column5: He looks around the room, and is quickly let down.
column6: 他环顾房间，很快便失望了。

column5: Of course there isn't. You know, I thought it'd be a given.\nAlgus is all alone, with nothing but his books, and imagination.\nIf there's any type of person who'd live off of wine, it'd be him.
column6: 当然没有。你知道吗，我本以为这是理所当然的。\n阿尔古斯孤身一人，只有书和想象相伴。\n要说哪种人会靠酒过活，那肯定是他。

column5: It's a lonely life, being a writer. It really is.\nYou pour so much emotion into it, that you almost run out.\nEveryone thinks you're giving them the cold shoulder, but you're not.
column6: 当个作家，是种孤独的日子。真的是这样。\n你投入了太多情感，以至于几乎耗尽了自己。\n所有人都以为你在给他们冷脸，可你并没有。

column5: Writing is art. Nobody questions the secluded painter, you know?\nBut the second you close yourself off to write — you're troubled.\nSo many people see it as a \"joke\" of a career choice.
column6: 写作是门艺术。没人会去质疑一个离群索居的画家，你知道吗？\n可你一闭关写作——就成了有毛病的人。\n太多人把这种职业选择当成一个“笑话”。

column5: I almost let that get me down when I was younger.\nThey told me that a writer could never make a decent living.\nI could've easily given up. But instead, I created a legacy.
column6: 我年轻时差点被这话击垮。\n他们告诉我，作家永远无法体面地谋生。\n我本可以轻易放弃。但我没有，反而创下了一份传世之作。

column5: He lets out a loud sigh.
column6: 他长叹了一声。

column5: And that's what scares me.\nEven when I give up the swindling life, that won't be enough.\nEveryone will remember me for who I was — not who I am.
column6: 而这正是我害怕的。\n即便我放弃行骗的生活，那也还不够。\n所有人都会记住过去的我——而不是现在的我。

column5: And let's be honest. I'm not one of the good guys.\nI stole secrets, sold them, and ruined people's lives.\nLook at what I did to The Rebellion. That's unforgivable.
column6: 而且老实说，我算不上什么好人。\n我偷取秘密，再转手贩卖，毁了别人的人生。\n看看我对反抗军做过的事。那是不可原谅的。

column5: He looks away from me, and shakes his head.
column6: 他把目光从我身上移开，摇了摇头。

column5: I think I might die during the attack, [firstname].\nThere's no place for me in your new, peaceful world.\nEven if I change — the harm I did will always haunt me.
column6: 我觉得我可能会死在这场进攻中，[firstname]。\n在你那个和平的新世界里，没有我的位置。\n即便我改变了——我造成的伤害也会永远缠着我。

column5: He steps forward, and wraps his arms around me.
column6: 他上前一步，张开双臂抱住了我。

column5: I know we want to be together, but it's difficult.\nYou don't understand how many people I've wronged in the past.\nIf they seek revenge, they might just target the people I love.
column6: 我知道我们想要在一起，但这很难。\n你不明白我过去得罪过多少人。\n如果他们来寻仇，可能会把矛头对准我爱的人。

column5: And I don't want you to get hurt just because I was a bad person.\nI could turn a new leaf, but that doesn't mean my enemies will, too.\nIf we're together, you might always be a target. It makes me scared.
column6: 我不想你因为我是个坏人而受到伤害。\n我可以改过自新，但这并不意味着我的仇敌也会。\n如果我们在一起，你可能永远都是目标。这让我害怕。

column5: I smile, and return the hug. So what if Pro's enemies would give us hell?{w}\nIf the rulers of the world can't take us down — how could anyone else?{w}\nI know he's panicking, so I softly run my hands through his hair.
column6: 我微笑着回抱住他。普洛的仇敌会让我们日子难过又怎样？{w}\n如果这个世界的统治者都扳不倒我们——还有谁能？{w}\n我知道他正惊慌失措，便轻轻用手抚过他的头发。

column5: We're in this together. We don't run away when things get difficult.{w}\nWe'll stand strong, and handle it as a team. That's what I truly want.
column6: 我们同在一条船上。遇到困难，我们不会逃避。{w}\n我们会坚强地并肩而立，作为一个团队去应对。这才是真正想要的。

column5: Together...?
column6: 一起……？

column5: Yeah, until the end.
column6: 对，直到最后。

column5: I just fear that the end is closer than we think.\nIf this could be our last night together — what do I do?\nHow do I press forward knowing that we might lose each other?
column6: 我只是怕这终点比我们以为的更近。\n如果这可能是我们共度的最后一晚——我该怎么办？\n明知我们可能失去彼此，我又该如何继续前行？

column5: If this could be our last moment together, then we make it count.{w}\nI step forward, and gently push Pro against the wall behind him.{w}\nHe blushes, and looks around the room, embarrassed.
column6: 如果这可能是我们共度的最后一刻，那就让它有意义吧。{w}\n我上前一步，轻轻把普洛按在他身后的墙上。{w}\n他脸红了，尴尬地环顾着房间。

column5: A-are you sure...?\nI mean, I don't want to rush anything.\nI've never really done this with anyone before.
column6: 你、你确定吗……？\n我是说，我不想操之过急。\n我以前从没和任何人做过这种事。

column5: I don't think it's rushing. It's seizing the moment.{w}\nEspecially given the fact that this could be the end.{w}\nNow, more than ever, we should do what we want.
column6: 我不觉得这是操之过急。这是把握当下。{w}\n尤其考虑到这可能是终局。{w}\n此刻，我们比任何时候都更该去做自己想做的事。

column5: You're right. I want this.
column6: 你说得对。我想要这个。

column5: He gulps, nervous.
column6: 他咽了口唾沫，很紧张。

column5: And if we both survive, you'll still want {i}me{/i}?\nWe can put the past behind us, and tackle the future?\nI've done a lot, you know. So your forgiveness means—
column6: 那如果我们都活下来，你还会想要{i}我{/i}吗？\n我们能放下过去，一起面对未来吗？\n要知道，我做过很多事。所以你的原谅意味着——

column5: After a quick nod, I press my lips against his.{w}\nKeeping him pressed against the wall, we continue to kiss.{w}\nAfter pledging myself to him — we gave each other a night to remember.
column6: 我迅速点了点头，然后把唇贴上了他的。{w}\n我将他抵在墙上，我们继续亲吻。{w}\n在向他许下承诺之后——我们给了彼此一个难忘的夜晚。

column5: He turns away, and I see him tremble a little in fright.
column6: 他转过身去，我看见他有些害怕地微微发抖。

column5: I want to help you make this world a better place, [firstname].\nBut you don't understand how many people I've wronged in the past.\nIf they seek revenge, they might just target you and all of my friends.
column6: 我想帮你把这个世界变得更美好，[firstname]。\n但你不明白我过去得罪过多少人。\n如果他们来寻仇，可能会把矛头对准你和我的所有朋友。

column5: And I don't want anybody to get hurt because I was a bad person.\nI could turn a new leaf, sure — but that doesn't mean my enemies will.\nIf I stay by your side, you and all of our friends will always be targets.
column6: 我不想任何人因为我是个坏人而受到伤害。\n我确实可以改过自新——但这并不意味着我的仇敌也会。\n如果我留在你身边，你和我们所有朋友都会永远成为靶子。

column5: I put a hand on his shoulder, and help him turn around.{w}\nSo what if his enemies tries to give us hell? We could handle it.{w}\nIf the rulers of the world can't take us down, how could anyone else?
column6: 我把一只手搭在他肩上，帮他转过身来。{w}\n他的仇敌想让我们日子难过又如何？我们能应付。{w}\n如果这个世界的统治者都扳不倒我们，还有谁能？

column5: You're right...
column6: 你说得对……

column5: We're all one big family. In this together, until the end.
column6: 我们就像一个大家庭。同舟共济，直到最后。

column5: I just fear that the end is closer than we think.\nI don't know what I'd do if I lost any of you during the final battle.\nI lost my family once. How can I expect to handle that again?
column6: 我只是怕这终点比我们以为的更近。\n如果在最后的战斗中我失去了你们中的任何一个，我不知道该怎么办。\n我曾经失去过一次家人。我怎么能指望自己再承受一次？

column5: I tell him not to worry, and that everything would be fine.{w}\nWe have a solid battle plan, and I have The Blade of Exodus.{w}\nThere wasn't anything we could do to stand a better chance at winning.
column6: 我告诉他别担心，一切都会好起来的。{w}\n我们有周密的作战计划，而我有流亡之刃。{w}\n我们已没有别的办法能让自己胜算更大。

column5: I guess that's true. Sorry, I was just freaking out.\nThat seems to be a running theme out there in the atrium.\nIt's impossible to look death in the face, and have no regrets.
column6: 我想也是。抱歉，我刚刚就是有点慌。\n中庭那边似乎也弥漫着这种情绪。\n直面死亡时，不可能毫无遗憾。

column5: But, if you want me to help you rule after this war — I will.\nAnything you need, I'll always be there to serve you, [firstname].\nHopefully I can earn a pardon for all the laws I've broken in the past.
column6: 不过，如果战后你想让我帮你治理——我愿意。\n无论你需要什么，我都会随时为你效力，[firstname]。\n但愿我能为自己过去犯下的所有罪行求得赦免。

column5: That would be easy. He's already done a lot to help us.{w}\nHe was responsible for our Alarinthian alliance, hands down.{w}\nHe's done his best to atone, and in my opinion, he succeeded.
column6: 那很容易。他已经帮了我们很多。{w}\n毫无疑问，阿拉林西亚的联盟正是他促成的。{w}\n他已尽力赎罪，在我看来，他成功了。

column5: So I pardon him right here and now.{w}\nOn the dawn of our final battle, he'd become a new man.{w}\nNo longer a swindler, but a trusted servant of The New Monarchy.
column6: 所以我此刻就赦免他。{w}\n在决战的前夜，他变成了一个全新的人。{w}\n不再是骗子，而是新王权值得信赖的臣仆。

column5: [firstname]...?
column6: [firstname]……？

column5: He looks shocked, almost in disbelief.{w}\nBut rather than question it, he nods, smiling.
column6: 他看上去很震惊，几乎难以置信。{w}\n但他没有再追问，只是微笑着点了点头。

column5: Thank you...
column6: 谢谢你……

column5: I send him off, but not before telling him one important fact.{w}\nAny enemy of him, is an enemy of The Monarchy, and will be dealt with.{w}\nHe thanks me yet again, and leaves with a resolve stronger than ever before.
column6: 我送他离开，但在此之前，我告诉了他一件重要的事。{w}\n任何与他为敌的人，就是与王权为敌，必将受到处置。{w}\n他再次向我道谢，带着前所未有的坚定离开了。

column5: As I'm lost in thought, a knock at the door jolts me awake.{w}\nWithout hesitation, I open it up, and Ulric steps inside.{w}\nHe seems calm. He's seen tons of battle in his lifetime.
column6: 正当我陷入沉思，门外的敲门声把我惊醒。{w}\n我毫不犹豫地打开门，乌尔里克走了进来。{w}\n他看上去很平静。他这一生经历过无数战斗。

column5: Hey, [firstname]. I just wanted to come see you.\nWe won't be getting much sleep tonight, after all.
column6: 嘿，[firstname]。我只是想来看看你。\n毕竟今晚我们都不会睡得太安稳。

column5: It's true; and I don't blame anybody for it.{w}\nEspecially Ulric. We were fighting his former masters.{w}\nThis would be harder on him than it would be for us.
column6: 确实如此；我谁都不怪。{w}\n尤其是乌尔里克。我们要对抗的，是他曾经的主人。{w}\n这对他来说，比对我们要艰难得多。

column5: I can't stop thinking about our visit to Alarinthia.\nYou know, I broke your nose, and I feel awful about that.\nBut I couldn't let you get in the way, and compromise our plan.
column6: 我一直在想我们去阿拉林西亚的那次拜访。\n你知道吗，我打碎了你的鼻子，我为此很难受。\n但我不能让你挡道，破坏我们的计划。

column5: It {i}needed{/i} to come down to just Pro and myself.\nIt was the only way that we could guarantee our victory.\nI guess I came here seeking your forgiveness. I feel foolish, though.
column6: 那件事{i}必须{/i}只由普洛和我两个人来做。\n那是我们确保胜利的唯一办法。\n我想，我来这里是想求得你的原谅。可我这样显得很傻。

column5: Your forgiveness was implied when you removed that curse from me.\nI mean, you wouldn't do something like that if you resented me, right?\nBut still — having it implied? It's not the same as hearing you say it.
column6: 当你为我解除了那道诅咒，其实就已经表明了你的原谅。\n我是说，如果你怨恨我，是不会那样做的，对吧？\n但即便如此——仅仅是被默认？那和亲耳听到你说出口终究不同。

column5: I can tell what he's after, so I tell him that he's forgiven.{w}\nTo be honest, it's the last thing on my mind right now.{w}\nIf it secured us our Draconic Alliance, it was worth it.
column6: 我明白他想要什么，便告诉他，我原谅他了。{w}\n说实话，这是我此刻最不放在心上的一件事。{w}\n如果它为我们换来了巨龙同盟，那就值得。

column5: That's the thing, though. Forgiveness shouldn't come so easy.\nWhen you're on the throne, you'll need to learn how to punish.\nI lied to you. I hurt you. I shouldn't deserve your forgiveness.
column6: 可问题就在这儿。原谅不该来得这么轻易。\n等你坐上王座，你得学会如何惩罚。\n我对你撒了谎。我伤害了你。我不该配得上你的原谅。

column5: Then why did he come here asking for it...?{w}\nI tell him that he deserves forgiveness because he meant no ill will.{w}\nHe did what he did out of necessity. To help further our cause, and win.
column6: 那他又为什么来这儿求它……？{w}\n我告诉他，他值得原谅，因为他并无恶意。{w}\n他所做的一切都是出于必要。是为了推进我们的事业，赢得胜利。

column5: I guess what I'm trying to say is — you're lucky it was just your nose.\nIn that moment, I would've done whatever I deemed necessary, [firstname].\nAnd given the opportunity, I would do it again. I would go as far as I needed.
column6: 我想说的是——你只是鼻梁断了，已经算走运了。\n那一刻，我会做出我认为必要的一切，[firstname]。\n若有需要，我还会再做一次。我会尽全力去做。

column5: Do you still think I'm worthy of your forgiveness?\nWho knows what I might have to do during the final battle.\nThe fate of the world is in the balance. I can't hold back.
column6: 你现在还觉得我配得上你的原谅吗？\n谁知道在最后的战斗里我会做出什么。\n世界的命运悬于一线。我不能有所保留。

column5: What's gotten into him all of a sudden...?{w}\nHe's acting odd, but I try not to bring it to his attention.{w}\nFor all I know, he's just anxious about the upcoming battle.
column6: 他这是突然怎么了……？{w}\n他行为古怪，但我尽量不点破。{w}\n据我所知，他只是为即将到来的战斗感到焦虑。

column5: But still, I tell him that he's forgiven.{w}\nI can't hold him accountable for things he hasn't done.{w}\nWhat he {i}has{/i} done, however, he's more than made up for.
column6: 但即便如此，我还是告诉他，我原谅他了。{w}\n我不能为他还没做过的事追究他。{w}\n而他所{i}做{/i}过的事，早已将功补过。

column5: Alright. As long as we're both on the same page.\nI expect the same from you. Don't hold back in any way.\nIf I'm in danger, don't stop to help me. You have your goal.
column6: 好吧。只要我们的想法一致就行。\n我也期望你同样如此。任何方面都不要有所保留。\n如果我陷入危险，别停下来救我。你有你的目标。

column5: He wants me to just leave him for dead...?
column6: 他想让我就这么丢下他等死……？

column5: I know what I was getting into when you removed my curse.\nI'm vulnerable — for the first time in thousands of years.\nBut while I'm vulnerable, I also feel {i}alive{/i}, [firstname].
column6: 你解除我诅咒的时候，我就知道自己在做什么。\n我很脆弱——这是几千年来第一次。\n但在我脆弱的同时，我也觉得自己{i}活着{/i}，[firstname]。

column5: It's amazing how much the possibility of death can motivate us.\nIn some ways, that's what drives us to accomplish our goals.\nWithout some sort of end, there's no time for us to seize.
column6: 死亡的可能性竟能如此激励我们，真是不可思议。\n从某种角度说，正是它驱使我们去实现目标。\n若没有某种终局，就没有值得我们去把握的时光。

column5: He would know better than me.{w}\nI don't think even he knows how old he is.{w}\nAt that point, the years would start to blur together.
column6: 这一点他比我更清楚。{w}\n我想连他自己都不知道自己活了多久。{w}\n到了那个份上，岁月大概早已模糊成一片。

column5: His demeanor makes sense, now that he's facing his mortality.{w}\nHis actions have consequences that could affect the rest of his life.{w}\nIn the past, no matter what he did, he could just outlive repercussion.
column6: 他如今要面对自己的死亡，这样的态度也说得通了。{w}\n他的行为会带来可能影响他余生的后果。{w}\n过去，无论他做什么，他都能熬过任何后果。

column5: I tell him I'll do it. I'll leave him behind, only if it's necessary.{w}\nI do have my goal — but part of that is ensuring my comrades stay alive.{w}\nThe pledge seems to satisfy him enough, and he changes the subject.
column6: 我告诉他我会照做。只会在必要的时候丢下他。{w}\n我确实有我的目标——但其中也包括确保同伴们活下来。{w}\n这个承诺似乎让他足够满意，于是他换了话题。

column5: Thank you, [firstname].\nI knew you'd be strong enough to make the tough decisions.\nSince we met, I've seen nothing but a capable ruler in you.
column6: 谢谢你，[firstname]。\n我就知道你有足够坚强，能做出艰难的抉择。\n从我们相识起，我在你身上看到的只有一位能干的统治者。

column5: And that was before the attack on the Rebel HQ.\nRemember back in Valinorth, when we were at Peregrino?\nYou've been leading this world for much longer than you think.
column6: 而那还是在袭击反抗军总部之前。\n还记得在瓦利诺斯，我们在佩雷格里诺的时候吗？\n你领导这个世界的时间，比你想象的要久得多。

column5: And I have to say, I agree with your choices.\nKeeping Peregrino as a tavern? I thought about that for a while.\nAnybody who values alcohol that much is good in {i}my{/i} books.
column6: 我得说，我赞同你的选择。\n把佩雷格里诺保留为酒馆？我想了很久。\n任何如此看重酒的人，在{i}我{/i}看来都不错。

column5: And I have to say, I agree with your choices.\nTurning Peregrino into a barracks to protect your homeland?\nAnybody who cares about their people that much is a great leader.
column6: 我得说，我赞同你的选择。\n把佩雷格里诺改成兵营来保卫你的家园？\n任何如此关心自己人民的人，都是了不起的领袖。

column5: He smiles at me, and places a hand on my shoulder.
column6: 他冲我笑了笑，一只手搭在我肩上。

column5: When I look back on times like that, I realize how far we've come.\nComplete strangers — to lovers. And it all happened so fast.\nI wasn't expecting it, but that's how I know it's real.
column6: 回首那样的时刻，我才意识到我们走了多远。\n从素不相识——到相爱。一切都发生得那么快。\n我未曾料到，但正因如此，我才知道这是真的。

column5: Some people pursue love, like it'll make them whole.\nBut it's not right to place a burden like that on somebody else.\nI think you can only really enjoy love, when you love yourself first.
column6: 有些人追寻爱情，仿佛它能让自己变得完整。\n但把这样的重担加在别人身上是不对的。\n我觉得，只有当先学会爱自己，你才能真正享受爱情。

column5: And that's what you helped me do, [firstname].\nIt's like — the more I know about you, the more I know about myself.\nAnd I don't want to stop learning. I want it for the rest of my life.
column6: 而这正是你帮我做到的，[firstname]。\n就像——我越了解你，就越了解自己。\n我不想停下这份学习。我想要它伴我一生。

column5: I'm just grateful that now, it's a life I deem worth living.\nIf I don't lose it on the battlefield, then I want to spend it with {i}you{/i}.\nBeing able to grow old, and say goodbye? It's an odd thing to desire.
column6: 我只感激，如今我认定这是值得一活的人生。\n如果我能在战场上保住它，那我愿意和你{i}一起{/i}度过。\n能够慢慢变老，然后道别？渴望这种事有些古怪。

column5: But when you lose the ability to die, you start to miss it.\nIn fact, you can almost forget what it's like to feel alive.\nI did — at least until I first laid eyes on you.
column6: 可当你失去了死亡的能力，就会开始怀念它。\n事实上，你几乎会忘记活着是什么感觉。\n我就是如此——至少，直到我第一次看见你。

column5: He takes the hand off of my shoulder, and laughs.
column6: 他把手从我肩上移开，笑了起来。

column5: I'm going to quit while I'm ahead.\nDon't want to give away my wedding vows.\nThis is actually some prime material, now that I think about it.
column6: 我还是见好就收吧。\n可不想把自己的婚礼誓词提前说光。\n仔细想想，这些可都是绝佳的素材。

column5: Pulling me into a hug, he places a kiss on the top of my head.
column6: 他把我拉进怀里，在我头顶落下一吻。

column5: When I look back on times like that, I realize how far we've come.\nComplete strangers — to loyal comrades, ready to kill false Gods.\nI never would've expected this, but it's not an unwelcome change.
column6: 回首那样的时刻，我才意识到我们走了多远。\n从素不相识——到忠诚的同伴，随时准备弑杀伪神。\n我从未料想到会这样，但这并非不受欢迎的改变。

column5: I always pledged myself to Damek, but the tables have shifted.\nThe sword arm meant for him, now belongs to you, [firstname].\nI will protect you, and do my best to help you liberate this world.
column6: 我一直向达梅克宣誓效忠，但如今局势已经变了。\n原本为他挥剑的手臂，如今属于你了，[firstname]。\n我会保护你，尽力帮你解放这个世界。

column5: It's the least I can do, after all. You removed this curse from me.\nNow that I can die, it's almost as if — I know what it's like to be alive.\nTo live, {i}without{/i} feeling alive? I wouldn't wish that on my worst enemy.
column6: 毕竟，这只是我起码该做的。你为我解除了那道诅咒。\n既然如今我能死去，那几乎就像——我知道了活着是什么感觉。\n活着，却{i}感受不到{/i}活着？我不愿把这诅咒加诸最恨的敌人。

column5: Yet, The Triumvirate hands it out so freely.\nThey disguise the tightest shackles as the path to freedom.\nAnd in our blindness, we accept it without hesitation.
column6: 然而，三人执政团却如此随意地将它施予他人。\n他们把最紧的枷锁伪装成通往自由的道路。\n而我们在盲目之中，毫不犹豫地接受了它。

column5: He shakes his head, as if throwing away thoughts of the enemy.{w}\nA moment later, the hand on my shoulder is removed.
column6: 他摇了摇头，仿佛要把对敌人的念头甩开。{w}\n片刻之后，他搭在我肩上的手移开了。

column5: The Rebellion, however, strives for {i}true{/i} freedom.\nSalus, and Damek? We have them to thank for everything.\nEven you wouldn't have realized your full potential without them.
column6: 然而反抗军追求的，是{i}真正{/i}的自由。\n萨卢斯，还有达梅克？这一切都要感谢他们。\n若不是他们，连你也不会意识到自己真正的潜力。

column5: That's true. It was Salus who broke Valinorth's non-partisan stance.{w}\nHe helped seize the blade, and deliver it to me. He knew about my power.{w}\nHe may not have known about The Monarchy, but he knew enough.
column6: 确实如此。正是萨卢斯打破了瓦利诺斯不结盟的立场。{w}\n他帮忙夺下刃，又把它交给了我。他知道我的力量。{w}\n他或许不知道王权的存在，但他知道的已经够多了。

column5: It feels weird saying this, but you might be my first real friend.\nThose are hard to come by when you're serving The Triumvirate.\nAnd harder still, to come by, when you close yourself off to the world.
column6: 说这话感觉有点怪，但你可能是我第一个真正的朋友。\n在效力三人执政团的时候，这种人很难遇到。\n而当你把自己封闭起来时，就更难遇到了。

column5: I'm not used to friends. I'm used to people who take advantage of me.\nWhether it's my strength, or my sense of honor. They've all been used.\nWhen people learn who you are, they might try and use you too, [firstname].
column6: 我不习惯有朋友。我习惯的是那些利用我的人。\n无论是我的力量，还是我的荣誉感。它们都被利用过。\n当人们弄清你的身份，他们可能也会想利用你，[firstname]。

column5: But when it comes to you, I know that my strength and honor {i}aren't{/i} misguided.\nYou can trust me to have your back, in the final battle, and beyond. I promise.\nFor once, I've found a cause I'd be happy to both live, {i}and{/i} die for.
column6: 但对你，我知道我的力量与荣誉{i}没有{/i}用错地方。\n你可以相信我会在最后的战斗以及那之后，始终守在你身后。我保证。\n这一次，我终于找到了一个我既愿意为之生、{i}也{/i}愿意为之死的目标。

column5: He smiles, a real, genuine smile.
column6: 他笑了，一个真实、真诚的笑容。

column5: Let's continue this after the battle, alright?\nUnfinished business is just one more reason to survive.\nIn times like these, we need as many of those as we can get.
column6: 我们等战后再接着聊，好吗？\n未了的事，本身就是多一个活下去的理由。\n在这样的时刻，这样的理由越多越好。

column5: I nod, and see him out of my room.{w}\nHe seems a bit different, but I don't blame him.{w}\nAnybody would change when given the ability to die.
column6: 我点点头，送他出了房间。{w}\n他看起来有些不一样了，但我不怪他。{w}\n任何人在获得死亡的能力后，都会改变。

column5: I'm just thankful that he's staying optimistic about it.{w}\nIt makes me realize that he really wanted it. It wasn't a hasty decision.{w}\nAnd with that optimism, I know he'd survive, and live a long, happy life.
column6: 我只是庆幸他对此依然保持乐观。{w}\n这让我意识到，他是真心想要的。这不是草率的决定。{w}\n带着这份乐观，我知道他会活下来，并度过漫长而幸福的一生。

column5: I invite Damek over to my private room, and he looks around, astonished.{w}\nEven though he's seen it before, he acts as if it's the first time.{w}\nI don't blame him. This room surely is a sight to behold.
column6: 我邀请达梅克来我私人的房间，他环顾四周，惊叹不已。{w}\n尽管他以前见过，却表现得像是头一回。{w}\n我不怪他。这房间确实令人叹为观止。

column5: I invite Damek over to my private room, and he looks around, astonished.{w}\nIt's almost like he's never seen anything so fancy before.{w}\nOr maybe, didn't expect such beauty out of Balteus.
column6: 我邀请达梅克来我私人的房间，他环顾四周，惊叹不已。{w}\n他几乎像是从没见过这么华丽的场面。{w}\n又或许，是没想到巴尔泰乌斯会有这般美景。

column5: What a sight, [firstname].\nI assume this is where Algus would normally sleep.\nBut he's not going anywhere in his current state.
column6: 真是好景致，[firstname]。\n我猜这里原本是阿尔古斯睡觉的地方。\n但以他现在的状况，他哪儿也去不了。

column5: I talked to him for a while, and he seems... unstable.\nYears of serving The Triumvirate will do that to you, I guess.\nEven after I told him what Howl was, he still lives in ignorance.
column6: 我和他聊了一会儿，他看起来……很不稳定。\n我猜，多年效命于三人执政团，会把人变成这样。\n即便我告诉他豪尔是什么，他仍选择活在无知之中。

column5: Well, maybe ignorance isn't the right word.\nHe knows what The Triumvirate is, and still chooses to serve them.\nYou know, I wonder how the people will react when they find out.
column6: 好吧，也许“无知”这词用得不对。\n他知道三人执政团是什么，却依然选择效忠他们。\n你知道吗，我在想，民众得知真相后会作何反应。

column5: Algus knows, and chose not to rebel, {i}or{/i} fight back.\nMaybe our victory here will just be the start of another battle.\nNot literally, of course. But we'll fight to show everyone the truth.
column6: 阿尔古斯知道，却既没有反抗，{i}也{/i}没有还击。\n也许我们在这里的胜利，只是另一场战斗的开始。\n当然，不是字面意义上的战斗。但我们会奋力让所有人看清真相。

column5: He shifts, almost like he's feeling a bit uncomfortable.
column6: 他动了动身子，仿佛有些不自在。

column5: I have to ask you something, though.\nIf the people don't respect your rule, what will you do?\nWill you work hard to earn it? Or will you demand it through fear?
column6: 不过，我得问你一件事。\n如果民众不尊重你的统治，你会怎么做？\n你会努力去赢得它？还是用恐惧去索取它？

column5: Good. That's what I like to hear.\nWe can't resort to methods used by our enemy.\nIf we did that, then nothing would change in the end.
column6: 很好。这正是我想听到的。\n我们不能用敌人用过的手段。\n如果我们那样做，那到头来什么都不会改变。

column5: Just — don't go down in history as a pushover.\nEven the best ruler needs to put their foot down, you know?\nTrying to give everybody what they want would just drive you mad.
column6: 只是——别在历史上留下个软柿子的名声。\n再好的统治者有时也得强势起来，你知道吗？\n试图满足所有人的要求，只会把你逼疯。

column5: I suppose you're right. \nBut don't lean too heavily on the side of fear.\nYou don't want to become the enemy we're taking down.
column6: 我想你说得对。\n但别过度偏向恐惧那一边。\n你不会想变成我们正在扳倒的那种敌人。

column5: They definitely rule though fear, [firstname].\nBut The Rebellion isn't afraid to speak up, and shut them down.\nSometimes using fear just inspires others to contest your rule.
column6: 他们确实是靠恐惧统治的，[firstname]。\n但反抗军不怕站出来，也不怕将他们推翻。\n有时用恐惧，反而会激起更多人反抗你的统治。

column5: I don't know about that, [firstname].\nAt that point, what makes you different than The Triumvirate?\nKeep an open mind, and let's tackle this together after we win.
column6: 这我可说不准，[firstname]。\n真到那一步，你和三人执政团又有什么分别？\n保持开放的心态，等我们赢了再一起解决这事。

column5: You know, we need to be {i}very{/i} careful with what we do next.\nOur actions will echo, and we can't display {i}any{/i} bad intentions.\nIf we do, then those echoes could just inspire more rebellion.
column6: 你知道吗，接下来的所作所为，我们必须{i}非常{/i}谨慎。\n我们的行为会激起回响，我们不能流露出{i}任何{/i}恶意。\n否则，那些回响只会激起更多的反叛。

column5: He shrugs, realizing it's probably a good idea to change the subject.{w}\nWe need to {i}secure{/i} victory before deciding what we'd do with it.{w}\nIt's clear that he wants to avoid talking about the upcoming battle.
column6: 他耸耸肩，意识到换个话题大概是个好主意。{w}\n我们得先{i}确保{/i}胜利，再决定要怎么用它。{w}\n显然，他想避开谈论即将到来的战斗。

column5: It just makes me wonder who The Triumvirate really is.\nThey aren't Gods — and I doubt that they made The Blade of Exodus.\nThere's a chance that they're just like us. Using power to achieve their goals.
column6: 这让我不禁想，三人执政团究竟是什么来头。\n他们不是神——我也怀疑流亡之刃是他们造的。\n有可能，他们和我们一样。用力量来达成自己的目标。

column5: And they say that power corrupts. You've heard that, right?\nWhat if they were just like us in the past? What'll happen next?\nWill we just go on to become tyrants that the people despise?
column6: 人们说权力会腐蚀人心。你听说过吧？\n如果他们过去也和我们一样呢？接下来又会怎样？\n我们会不会也变成被民众唾弃的暴君？

column5: I shake my head. We wouldn't stoop so low.
column6: 我摇了摇头。我们不会堕落到那种地步。

column5: Nobody starts their journey at the peak power, [firstname].\nThe Triumvirate wasn't born into this role. They fought for it.\nIt's even likely that they took down foes of their own, too.
column6: 没有谁一开始就站在权力的顶峰，[firstname]。\n三人执政团并非生来就担此角色。他们是靠拼杀争来的。\n甚至很可能，他们也扳倒过自己的敌人。

column5: But what foe would that be? And what was their goal...?\nWhat I'm trying to say is — I think the blade should be destroyed.\nOnce we achieve our goal, we have no use for it anymore — right?
column6: 但那会是什么样的敌人？他们的目标又是什么……？\n我想说的是——我认为这把刃应当被毁掉。\n一旦达成目标，它就再无用武之地了——对吧？

column5: If you keep it, you risk relying on its power.\nAnd I don't want to see what that does to you, [firstname].\nNot if it's even {i}anything{/i} close to what it's done to our enemies.
column6: 如果你留着它，就得承担依赖它力量的风险。\n我不想看到那会把你变成什么样，[firstname]。\n尤其是，如果它对我们敌人所做的事哪怕{i}有一丝{/i}会重演在你身上。

column5: I don't see any reason to keep it around after the war is over.\nSo tell me — if you get the chance to destroy it, will you?
column6: 我想不出战事结束后还有什么理由留着它。\n所以告诉我——若你有机会毁掉它，你会吗？

column5: Good. There's no place for a weapon like that in this world.\nI feel like whoever wields it, will be led down a dark path.\nI'd just hate to see that happen to you. I really would.
column6: 很好。这世上容不下那样的武器。\n我觉得，无论谁挥舞它，都会被引向一条黑暗的道路。\n我只是不愿看到那样的事发生在你身上。真的不愿。

column5: I don't know if that's a good idea, [firstname].\nWhoever wields that blade will be led down a dark path.\nThat's not a path I'd like to see you walk. I couldn't bear it.
column6: 我不确定那是不是个好主意，[firstname]。\n无论谁挥舞那把刃，都会被引向一条黑暗的道路。\n那不是我愿你走的路。我无法承受。

column5: He looks away from me, sad.
column6: 他把目光从我身上移开，神情悲伤。

column5: I just want to know what kind of hands the world will be left in.\nI'm just asking you these questions because I'm scared, you know.\nI might not survive the battle. I might not live to see your reign.
column6: 我只是想知道，这个世界最终会落入怎样的人手中。\n我问你这些，只是因为我在害怕，你知道吗。\n我可能活不过这场战斗。我可能活不到看见你统治的那一天。

column5: That much was true. Even my survival wasn't guaranteed.
column6: 这倒属实。连我能否活下来都毫无保证。

column5: I'd hate to lose each other, after how far we've come.\nBut we're about to fight The Triumvirate — so it's a real possibility.\nAll we really can do, is launch the final attack with no regrets at all.
column6: 我们走了这么远，我可不愿失去彼此。\n但我们即将对抗三人执政团——所以这确实是有可能的。\n我们真正能做的，就是毫无遗憾地发起最后的进攻。

column5: Now I have my fair share of regrets — that much is certain.\nBut with your help, I'd like to put some of them to rest.\nI wanted to do so back in Alarinthia, but I was scared.
column6: 说起来，我也有自己的一份遗憾——这一点毋庸置疑。\n但有你相助，我想了却其中的一些。\n我早在阿拉林西亚就想这么做，可我当时害怕。

column5: Back in Alarinthia...? What does he mean?
column6: 早在阿拉林西亚……？他是什么意思？

column5: You know that I have this fear of physical contact.\nWhen I saw everybody on the dance floor, I got jealous.\nIt seemed so easy, so natural for them. Why couldn't {i}I{/i} do that?
column6: 你知道的，我有这种惧怕身体接触的毛病。\n当我看到舞池里的所有人，我嫉妒了。\n对他们来说，一切似乎都那么轻松、那么自然。为什么{i}我{/i}做不到？

column5: They all looked so happy together. It was simply magical.\nAnd here I am, scared. I'm denying myself the pleasure of that magic.\nIf I keep doing that — I told myself — I'd die before I got the chance to feel it.
column6: 他们在一起时看上去那么快乐。那简直是种魔力。\n而我却在这里害怕。我在剥夺自己享受那份魔力的权利。\n我告诉自己——若我一直这样，我会在有机会感受之前就死去。

column5: But I want to feel it, Monarch. I want it more than anything.\nWhy does the simple thought of it make me shake in fear...?\nWhat did I do to deserve this? Why can't I be happy like them?
column6: 但我想感受它，君主。我想它胜过一切。\n为什么光是想想就让我恐惧得发抖……？\n我做了什么才落得如此？为什么我不能像他们那样快乐？

column5: I tell him that he can. He just needs to be brave enough.{w}\nThere may not be any music here, but I hold out my hands.{w}\nI ask him if he's willing to try. Just once, before the end of it all.
column6: 我告诉他他可以。他只需要鼓起勇气。{w}\n这里也许没有音乐，但我伸出了双手。{w}\n我问他是否愿意试一试。就在一切结束之前，试一次。

column5: He looks down at his own hands, and I see them tremble.{w}\nI know he's scared, but I tell him that I'm terrified as well.{w}\nWe could die, without ever knowing each other's touch.
column6: 他低头看着自己的手，我看见它们颤抖。{w}\n我知道他害怕，但我告诉他，我也同样恐惧。{w}\n我们可能会在从未知晓彼此温度的情况下死去。

column5: You're right. I could never live with myself if that happened.\nI want to know what it feels like, just in case I never get the chance again.\nSo — here we are — back in Alarinthia, that music playing in our ears.
column6: 你说得对。若真如此，我永远无法原谅自己。\n我想知道那是什么感觉，以防我再也没有机会。\n所以——你看——我们又回到了阿拉林西亚，那音乐在耳边回荡。

column5: I smile, with a nod, as he places his hands in mine.{w}\nHe's shaking, and scared. His eyes tear up, but he's smiling.{w}\nWithout saying a word, I pull him close, and hold him tight.
column6: 我微笑着点点头，他把双手放进了我的掌心。{w}\n他在发抖，很害怕。他眼眶湿润，却带着笑容。{w}\n我一言未发，将他拉近，紧紧抱住。

column5: I let him tame his emotions on his own.{w}\nIt takes a while, but his shaking slowly subsides.{w}\nHe's crying — but I can tell that it's not out of fright.
column6: 我任由他自己平复情绪。{w}\n过了好一会儿，他的颤抖才渐渐平息。{w}\n他在哭——但我看得出，那不是出于恐惧。

column5: We sway from side to side, as if we were dancing.{w}\nOur bodies are in sync with a melody that neither of us can hear.{w}\nIt's a beautiful moment, and it belongs to the two of us, as it will forever.
column6: 我们轻轻左右摇摆，仿佛在跳舞。{w}\n我们的身体与一段彼此都听不见的旋律同步律动。{w}\n这是美好的时刻，它属于我们两个人，也将永远如此。

column5: I love you...
column6: 我爱你……

column5: Damek sniffles, and rests his head against my shoulder.{w}\nI say that I love him too, and hold him even closer to my body.
column6: 达梅克抽了抽鼻子，把头靠在我的肩上。{w}\n我说我也爱他，把他抱得更紧。

column5: We stay like this until he's ready to leave. I've never seen him so happy.{w}\nIf he survives, then we'd spend our lives together in a similar happiness.{w}\nThis is the pledge I make to him as I see him off to prepare for the end.
column6: 我们就这样待着，直到他准备离开。我从没见过他这么开心。{w}\n若他能活下来，我们便会以同样的幸福共度一生。{w}\n这是我送他去为终局做准备时，向他许下的诺言。

column5: I'd hate for us to die, especially after how far we've come.\nBut we're about to fight The Triumvirate. It's a real possibility.\nAll we can really do, is ensure that we fight with no regrets.
column6: 我们走了这么远，我可不愿我们死去。\n但我们即将对抗三人执政团。这确实是有可能的。\n我们真正能做的，就是确保战斗时毫无遗憾。

column5: Now I have my fair share of regrets — that much is certain.\nBut with your help, I'd like to put some of them to rest.\nI've been wanting to for a while, but I'm just scared.
column6: 说起来，我也有自己的一份遗憾——这一点毋庸置疑。\n但有你相助，我想了却其中的一些。\n我想这么做已经有一阵子了，只是我一直害怕。

column5: Scared...? I think I know what he's getting at.
column6: 害怕……？我想我明白他的意思了。

column5: You know, shaking a hand is such a simple thing.\nYet I cower in fear whenever somebody offers it to me.\nEven the thought of it is enough to fill me with anxiety.
column6: 你知道吗，握手是件再简单不过的事。\n可每当有人向我伸出手，我都会恐惧地退缩。\n光是想到它，就足以让我焦虑不安。

column5: But you know what? So does fighting The Triumvirate.\nDespite that fact, I'm standing strong, and ready to fight.\nSo what do you say? To the fall of The Triumvirate...?
column6: 但你知道吗？对抗三人执政团也是如此。\n尽管如此，我依然坚强地站着，准备好去战斗。\n所以你说呢？为三人执政团的倒台……？

column5: He holds out his hand, and I can see it shaking.{w}\nI ask him if he's sure. This is a big deal, after all.
column6: 他伸出手，我能看见它在颤抖。{w}\n我问他是否确定。毕竟，这可不是小事。

column5: Of course I'm sure. It's time to get over this silly fear.\nYou know, we'll be dealing with a lot of people after this is over.\nNot being able to shake the hands of our subjects? That's not good.
column6: 我当然确定。是时候克服这种傻气的恐惧了。\n你知道，等这一切结束后，我们要和很多人打交道。\n连自己子民的手都握不了？那可不行。

column5: After all we've been through? I just think {i}you{/i} deserve the honors.\nAnd I can think of no better toast, than a toast to the fall of our enemies.\nSo like I said — let's do this — and move forward as stronger people.
column6: 经历了这一切之后？我只是觉得{i}你{/i}该享有这份殊荣。\n而我想不出比为我们敌人的倒台干杯更好的祝酒词了。\n所以就像我说的——来吧——让我们作为更坚强的人向前迈进。

column5: Yeah — as stronger people.{w}\nI shake his hand with a firm grip.{w}\nIf he was scared, he doesn't show it.
column6: 好——作为更坚强的人。{w}\n我稳稳地握住了他的手。{w}\n就算他曾经害怕，他也没有表现出来。

column5: This is all thanks to you, Monarch. It really is.\nYou told me to leave behind those memories of my past.\nAt first I thought it would dishonor the memory of my mother.
column6: 这一切都要感谢你，君主。真的。\n是你叫我放下那些过去的回忆。\n起初我以为，那会辜负我母亲的记忆。

column5: But I'm not forgetting about her. I could never do that.\nI'm just forgetting about the pain I felt on that fateful day.\nAnd with that gone — I can handle anything that comes my way.
column6: 但我并不是要忘记她。我永远做不到。\n我只是想忘掉在那命运攸关的一天所感受到的痛苦。\n一旦放下它——我就能应对任何向我袭来的事。

column5: He leaves the room with the biggest smile on his face.{w}\nI know that this was a big step for him, and he's incredibly proud.{w}
column6: 他脸上挂着最灿烂的笑容，离开了房间。{w}\n我知道这对他而言是巨大的一步，他无比自豪。{w}

column5: If he used that pride on the battlefield, then our enemies stood no chance.{w}\nJust like he said — The Triumvirate would fall — and we would be victorious.
column6: 如果他把这份自豪带到战场上，那我们的敌人就毫无胜算。{w}\n正如他所说——三人执政团会倒台——而我们将获得胜利。

column5: As I'm browsing random books, I hear a knock on my door.{w}\nIt's Howl. I let him in, and ask him how things are going.{w}\nI don't know why I asked. It's clear what the answer was.
column6: 正当我随手翻看书架上的书，门外传来了敲门声。{w}\n是豪尔。我让他进来，问他情况如何。{w}\n我不知道自己为什么要问。答案显而易见。

column5: They all worry. They fear that death will come for them.\nAn understandable fear, however. This is the end of our journey.\nWe will face more danger than ever before as we move forward.
column6: 他们都在担忧。他们害怕死亡会降临到自己头上。\n不过，这种恐惧可以理解。这是我们旅程的终点。\n随着我们继续前进，我们将面临前所未有的危险。

column5: Algus, however, isn't making things any easier.\nHe plants seeds of doubt in many of our soldiers, [firstname].\nWords are a writer's greatest weapon. A gag would be effective.
column6: 然而，阿尔古斯并没有让事情好过一点。\n他在我们许多士兵心中播下怀疑的种子，[firstname]。\n言语是作家最强大的武器。堵上他的嘴或许会有效。

column5: It's unclear if this is a joke, but it gets a smile from me regardless.
column6: 不清楚这是不是玩笑，但无论如何，它让我笑了。

column5: He says that we are the true enemy. The Monarchy.\nHe says that if you knew the truth of our people, you would run.\nYou would no longer fight for us — as we endangered innocent worlds.
column6: 他说我们才是真正的敌人。王权才是。\n他说，如果你知道我们族群的真相，你就会逃走。\n你将不再为我们而战——因为我们会危及无辜的世界。

column5: It is not true, however. His mind has been twisted beyond repair.\nBut many soldiers are starting to doubt. What if he is telling the truth?\nCould they save their lives by switching sides in the final moments?
column6: 然而，这不是真的。他的心智已被扭曲得无法修复。\n但许多士兵开始动摇了。万一他说的是真的呢？\n他们能否在最后关头倒戈，从而保住自己的性命？

column5: That is unacceptable. We couldn't afford any turncoats.
column6: 这绝不可接受。我们承受不起任何叛徒。

column5: The Monarchy made mistakes, as any group of people do.\nLike Damek said — mistakes are how we learn, and grow.\nBad choices, while bad, are our right as people to make.
column6: 王权犯过错，就像任何一群人都会犯错一样。\n正如达梅克所说——错误是我们学习和成长的方式。\n糟糕的选择虽然糟糕，却是我们作为人的权利。

column5: They cast us aside in a prison, taking away our ability to choose.\nAnd in doing so, they took away our ability to live in freedom.\nNo matter our crimes, this punishment is far too severe.
column6: 他们把我们丢进监狱，剥夺了我们选择的能力。\n如此，他们也就夺走了我们自由生活的权利。\n无论我们犯下什么罪，这惩罚都太过严酷。

column5: I agree, and I could never be turned against The Monarchy.{w}\nThe Triumvirate imprisoned them because they endangered worlds?{w}\nA hypocritical thing to say, as they hurt Alestia at the very same time.
column6: 我表示同意，我绝不会被策反去对抗王权。{w}\n三人执政团因为王权危及世界就囚禁了他们？{w}\n这话何其虚伪，因为他们同时也在伤害阿莱斯蒂亚。

column5: But, we must say — it was a battle that we lost fair and square.\nWe were so focused on our own future, that we lost sight of everyone else's.\nIt doesn't surprise us, that our \"perfect\" future came at the expense of others.
column6: 但我们必须承认——那是一场我们输得心服口服的战斗。\n我们太过专注于自己的未来，以至于忽视了其他人的未来。\n我们那“完美”的未来是建立在别人的代价之上，这并不令我们意外。

column5: If it leads to happiness in the end, how can you decide what cost is too high?\nThis is the line that all tyrants seem to walk in the early days of their rule.\nMany have fallen to the wrong side, [firstname]. We trust that you will not.
column6: 如果最终能带来幸福，你又如何判定什么代价算太高？\n这正是所有暴君在统治初期似乎都走过的那条界线。\n许多人失足跌向了错误的一侧，[firstname]。我们相信你不会。

column5: I nod. I don't see myself stooping to the level of the enemy anytime soon.
column6: 我点了点头。我看不出自己会有很快堕落到敌人那种地步。

column5: We know that Damek wishes to gift all this knowledge to the people.\nThese books capture almost the entire history of The Monarchy.\nThis may not be a good idea. They may read of our \"mistakes\".
column6: 我们知道达梅克想把这些知识全部送给民众。\n这些书记载了王权几乎全部的历史。\n这也许不是个好主意。他们可能会读到我们的“错误”。

column5: And those mistakes may just inspire future insurrections.\nWe think it may be best to destroy The Monarchy entirely.\nBurn these books, and remove the spirits from this body.
column6: 而那些错误，也许恰恰会激起未来的叛乱。\n我们认为，最好的做法或许是彻底抹除王权。\n烧掉这些书，把这些灵从这具躯体中移除。

column5: Wait, what...?{w}\nThat was certainly extreme.
column6: 等等，什么……？{w}\n这确实太极端了。

column5: These books shouldn't exist at all, [firstname].\nWe don't know why The Triumvirate keeps them lying around.\nIf our oppression was their goal, then they should've destroyed them.
column6: 这些书根本就不该存在，[firstname]。\n我们不明白三人执政团为什么把它们留在这里。\n如果他们的目的是压迫我们，那就该毁掉它们。

column5: Right now, they exist as a testament to our imprisonment.\nAs long as they remain intact, they will be only a harmful memory.\nThey should be destroyed. Allow my people, and our history, to rest.
column6: 如今，它们的存在是我们被囚禁的证明。\n只要它们完好无损，就只会是一段有害的记忆。\n它们应当被毁掉。让我的族人，和我们的历史，得以安息。

column5: This is all coming out of nowhere, but it makes sense.{w}\nHe is The Monarchy embodied. This must be a horrific sight for him.{w}\nHis entire culture, stolen. Imprisoned just like him and his people.
column6: 这一切来得毫无征兆，但说得通。{w}\n他就是王权的化身。这景象对他一定无比可怖。{w}\n他的整个文化被夺走。就像他和他的族人一样，被囚禁于此。

column5: This is why we ask that you look toward the future, [firstname].\nDo not concern yourself with who we were, or what we were like.\nOrder this library to be destroyed. Live life on your own terms.
column6: 这就是我们请求你放眼未来的原因，[firstname]。\n别再挂念我们曾经是谁，或我们曾是什么样子。\n下令毁掉这座图书馆。按照你自己的方式生活。

column5: I don't know what to say, so I just stare at him in silence.
column6: 我不知道该说什么，只能默默地注视着他。

column5: This started back during our journey into Eastcrown.\nThis body could not survive the cold. The spirits inside helped.\nBut in doing so, they died. We are weaker than we were back then.
column6: 这一切始于我们前往东冠的旅程。\n这具躯体无法在严寒中存活。体内的灵帮了忙。\n但正因如此，他们死了。我们比那时弱了许多。

column5: Weaker, but more in tune with everything around us.\nAlmost like a weight was lifted from our shoulders.\nWe would like you to lift this weight even further.
column6: 更弱了，但与周围的一切更加契合。\n仿佛有一副重担从我们的肩上卸下。\n我们希望你把这副重担卸得更彻底。

column5: Please, use that blade. Absorb the souls inside of us.\nLeave one behind — and let us feel what it is like to be alive.\nAfter the weight is gone from our shoulders, lift it from the world.
column6: 求你，用那把刃。吸取我们体内的灵魂。\n只留下一个——让我们感受活着是什么滋味。\n等这重担从我们肩上卸下后，再把它从这世上移去。

column5: He looks around the room, to the various books scattered about.
column6: 他环顾房间，看着散落各处的那些书。

column5: You must absorb these souls, and destroy the books.\nOnly then, will The Monarchy be truly removed from history.\nAs our mind will be better for it — so too, will the world itself.
column6: 你必须吸取这些灵魂，并毁掉这些书。\n唯有如此，王权才会真正从历史中被抹去。\n我们的心智会因此变得更好——这世界本身也一样。

column5: I don't know how to respond to what he's asking of me.{w}\nHe wants me to commit mass genocide against The Monarchy?{w}\nThis is all happening so fast, I'm unsure of how I should respond.
column6: 我不知道该如何回应他对我的请求。{w}\n他想让我对王权进行一场大屠杀？{w}\n这一切发生得太快，我不确定该如何回应。

column5: You would not be killing us. We have long since been dead.\nIt would be an act of mercy upon a group of oppressed people.\nWe can no longer live. The Triumvirate stole that right from us.
column6: 你不会是在杀我们。我们早已死去。\n这会是施予一群受压迫者的仁慈之举。\n我们再也无法活下去了。是三人执政团夺走了我们这份权利。

column5: But if you can take our spirits, and use it to power the blade?\nMaybe it will give you the edge you need to win this yourselves.\nWe may have lost — but that doesn't mean you need to, as well.
column6: 但如果你能取走我们的灵，用它来强化那把刃呢？\n也许它能给你们制胜所需的优势。\n我们也许输了——但这不意味着你们也会。

column5: These spirits may linger, and the books may remain.\nBut the truth of it is — we're dead. We need to be buried.\nOur very existence is born from a denial of that death.
column6: 这些灵也许会徘徊，这些书也许会留存。\n但事实是——我们已经死了。我们需要被埋葬。\n我们的存在，本就建立在对那死亡的否认之上。

column5: If you leave one soul, we will use this body to fight for you.\nWe may fall in combat, but nothing of value would be lost.\nWe cannot help our own people, so we must help yours.
column6: 如果你留下一个灵魂，我们就会用这具躯体为你而战。\n我们也许会在战斗中倒下，但不会有任何有价值的东西随之失去。\n我们帮不了自己的族人，那就必须帮你们的。

column5: I knew that eventually we'd have to tackle the nature of his existence.{w}\nBut I didn't expect to be confronted with it on the eve of the final battle.{w}\nHe wants to accept defeat. Have the souls removed, and books destroyed.
column6: 我知道，我们迟早要直面他存在的本质。{w}\n但我没料到会在决战前夜被摆到面前。{w}\n他想接受失败。让灵魂被移除，让书被毁掉。

column5: If I did that — there'd be no physical remains of The Monarchy.{w}\nI had spirits inside of me, but I was still my own person, able to live free.{w}\nWe're talking about the extinction of an entire group of people. I don't know.
column6: 如果我那样做——王权就不会留下任何实质的痕迹。{w}\n我体内曾有灵，但我仍是独立的个体，能够自由地活。{w}\n我们谈的是一整个族群的灭绝。我不知道。

column5: We understand if this is too much to ask, [firstname].\nBut we think this is the right course of action for everybody.\nDon't be scared to hurt us. You cannot harm what is already dead.
column6: 如果这要求太过分，我们能够理解，[firstname]。\n但我们认为，这对所有人来说都是正确的做法。\n别怕伤害我们。你无法伤害已经死去的东西。

column5: The spirits would be more useful in the blade, than this body.\nBut like we said, one can remain, to aid you in fighting.\nWhat do you say, [firstname]...? What will you do...?
column6: 这些灵在刃中，比在这具躯体里更有用。\n但正如我们所说，可以留下一个，助你战斗。\n你意下如何，[firstname]……？你会怎么做……？

column5: I agree to grant him his request.{w}\nI need this blade as strong as possible for the coming battle.{w}\nHis people may be lost, but they can still help us win this war.
column6: 我同意满足他的请求。{w}\n为了即将到来的战斗，我需要这把刃尽可能强大。{w}\n他的族人或许已经消逝，但他们仍能助我们赢下这场战争。

column5: Thank you, [firstname].\nDo not worry about the books, we will talk to Damek.\nBut know that you made the right choice, and rest easy.
column6: 谢谢你，[firstname]。\n不必担心那些书，我们会去和达梅克谈。\n但你要知道你做了正确的选择，安心吧。

column5: With a nod, I take out the blade, and hold it to his chest.{w}\nIt responds to my will, so I do my best to envision Howl's request.{w}\nLeave one soul to inhabit the body — and use the rest to power the blade.
column6: 我点点头，取出刃，抵在他的胸口。{w}\n它会回应我的意志，所以我尽力去构想豪尔的请求。{w}\n留下一个灵魂留在这具躯体里——用其余的来强化这把刃。

column5: I close my eyes, and try my hardest to make his dream a reality.{w}\nAfter a while, he takes a deep breath, and he seems a bit different.{w}\nThe blade didn't seem to \"activate\", but I guess I did what I needed to.
column6: 我闭上双眼，竭尽全力让他的愿望成真。{w}\n过了一会儿，他深吸一口气，看起来有些不一样了。{w}\n那把刃似乎并未“启动”，但我想我做了该做的事。

column5: Thank you. You did the right thing.\nIf you'll excuse us, we have more to take care of.\nThe final battle looms. There is much for all of us to do.
column6: 谢谢你。你做了正确的选择。\n恕我们先行告退，我们还有更多事要处理。\n决战临近。我们所有人都还有很多事要做。

column5: I nod, and see him out of my room.{w}\nI didn't expect to settle this one-on-one.{w}\nMaybe part of me wanted the input of others?
column6: 我点点头，送他出了房间。{w}\n我没料到会这样一对一地了结此事。{w}\n也许我内心有一部分想要别人的意见？

column5: However, I think things turned out for the best.{w}\nIf we maintained this secrecy, nobody would ever know.{w}\nI helped him — and he helped me. I was stronger than ever before.
column6: 不过，我觉得结果算是好的。{w}\n如果我们守住这个秘密，就永远不会有人知道。{w}\n我帮了他——他也帮了我。我变得比以往任何时候都强大。

column5: I couldn't do it. I couldn't be responsible for their extinction.{w}\nEven if they were already \"dead\". I couldn't be the one to end it.{w}\nI let him know that fact, and I can tell that he's immediately upset.
column6: 我做不到。我无法为他们的灭绝负责。{w}\n即便他们早已“死去”。我也不能成为终结这一切的人。{w}\n我把这一事实告诉了他，我看得出他立刻就沮丧起来。
