column5: Very well, [firstname].\nIt is a mistake, but it is your mistake to make.\nAfter all, you still live — free to make your own choices.
column6: 好吧，[firstname]。\n这是个错误，但这是你该犯的错误。\n毕竟，你还活着——自由地做出自己的选择。

column5: With a stern look on his face, he storms out of the room.{w}\nI can tell that I let him down, but I think I made the right choice.{w}\nAs I turn back to face the room, I keep telling myself that fact.
column6: 他脸色一沉，怒冲冲地走出了房间。{w}\n我看得出我让他失望了，但我认为我做了正确的选择。{w}\n当我转身再次面对房间时，我不断对自己重复着这一点。

column5: There's a knock at my door, more urgent sounding than I anticipated.{w}\nIt couldn't possibly be time to launch the attack. It must be something else.{w}\nAs soon as I open it, Sovy steps into the room, a look of anxiety on his face.
column6: 门外传来敲门声，比我预想的更加急促。{w}\n不可能是进攻的时候到了。一定是别的事。{w}\n我一开门，索维就走进房间，脸上带着焦虑的神色。

column5: Sorry, I just needed to get away from that atrium, [firstname].\nEverybody keeps telling me what to do, and it's getting on my nerves.\nI have no problem helping out your cause. But it's {i}my{/i} choice to do so.
column6: 抱歉，我只是需要从中庭躲开一下，[firstname]。\n所有人都没完没了地告诉我该做什么，这快把我逼疯了。\n帮助你的事业我毫无意见。但那是{i}我自己{/i}的选择。

column5: I followed enough orders while I was under The Triumvirate's control.\nJoining you and your army — I thought I'd finally be a free man.\nI mean, I guess I am. Ignore me, I'm just complaining.
column6: 我在三人执政团控制下的时候，已经听够了命令。\n加入你和你的军队——我以为我终于能做个自由人了。\n我是说，我想我现在是吧。别管我，我只是在抱怨。

column5: He shrugs, and starts wandering around the room.{w}\nI tell him that it's okay. He shouldn't have to follow orders here.{w}\nI give him free reign to do whatever he sees as the most useful.
column6: 他耸耸肩，开始在房间里踱步。{w}\n我告诉他没关系。在这里他不该被迫服从命令。{w}\n我让他全权决定做什么，只要他自己觉得最有用。

column5: You know, that's why I like you.\nYou're the only person who lets me do what I want.\nEverybody else keeps me at arm's length, commanding me.
column6: 你知道吗，这就是我喜欢你的原因。\n你是唯一一个让我随心所欲的人。\n其他人都跟我保持距离，对我发号施令。

column5: After all I've been through, I think I want to be the commander.\nI always thought I've been meant for more than what I was given.\nWhen I met you, and you accepted my offer — I knew I was right.
column6: 经历了这一切之后，我想当那个发号施令的人。\n我一直觉得，我生来就该得到比现有更多的东西。\n当我遇见你，你接受了我的提议——我就知道我没想错。

column5: At first, I only planned to help you until we took down Halin.\nBut we've grown so close, and your comrades are so accepting.\nI've never felt such a sense of belonging. A sense, perhaps, of family.
column6: 起初，我只打算帮你到扳倒哈林为止。\n但我们已经变得如此亲近，你的同伴又是如此包容。\n我从未有过这样的归属感。或许，是一种家的感觉。

column5: With a smile, he takes a book from the shelf, and opens it up.
column6: 他微笑着，从书架上取下一本书，翻开。

column5: You know, I've been reading about The Monarchy.\nThey seem to be more similar to The Triumvirate than we thought.\nThe Triumvirate demands perfection. The Monarchy sought the perfect future.
column6: 你知道吗，我一直在读关于王权的书。\n他们似乎和三人执政团比我们以为的更相似。\n三人执政团要求完美。王权追寻完美的未来。

column5: And it seems like neither group cared about what cost they paid.\nBut it's impossible to pinpoint the moment The Monarchy was imprisoned.\nMany of these books are dated with a system I'm unable to decipher.
column6: 而且看来，两个群体都不在乎自己付出了什么代价。\n但无法确定王权究竟是在何时被囚禁的。\n这些书里有许多的日期标示方式，我无法解读。

column5: So how advanced was The Monarchy when The Triumvirate took action?\nWere they silencing a real threat, or perhaps a potential threat...?\nOne is more acceptable than the other, but neither are just.
column6: 那么，当三人执政团出手时，王权有多先进？\n他们是在扼杀一个真实的威胁，还是潜在的威胁……？\n前者比后者更说得过去，但两者都不公正。

column5: I find myself wondering what would happen if someone opposed The Monarchy.\nWhat if somebody got in the way of them and their perfect future?\nWould they be killed, just like enemies of The Triumvirate?
column6: 我不禁想，如果当初有人反对王权会怎样。\n如果有人挡在他们和他们的完美未来之间呢？\n他们会被杀掉，就像三人执政团的敌人一样吗？

column5: And furthermore, how did they possess foresight to begin with?\nYou inherited it from them. But where did they get it from?\nSorry for rambling. There's just so many questions.
column6: 再者，他们究竟是怎么拥有预知能力的？\n你从他们那里继承了它。但他们又是从哪儿得来的？\n抱歉我絮絮叨叨。只是问题实在太多了。

column5: It might be best to just forget The Monarchy ever existed.\nStart over, from scratch, under the banner of The Rebellion.\nWhy reclaim a world for someone who would be your enemy?
column6: 也许，最好的做法就是忘了王权曾经存在。\n从零开始，以反抗军的旗帜重建一切。\n何必为了一群会成为你敌人的人，去夺回一个世界？

column5: The Triumvirate controls us, in an attempt to keep everything pure.\nThe Monarchy too, controlled their subjects. Just for a different reason.\nWe want to live free, right? Free to do what we want, and live how we want?
column6: 三人执政团控制我们，是为了保持一切纯净。\n王权也控制着他们的子民。只是出于不同的理由。\n我们想要自由地活着，对吧？自由地做想做的事，按想要的方式生活？

column5: I nod.
column6: 我点了点头。

column5: Why settle for the lesser of two evils?\nForget The Triumvirate. Forget The Monarchy.\nCarve your own path. Follow none tread by others.
column6: 为什么要退而求其次，在两个恶中选较轻的那个？\n忘掉三人执政团。忘掉王权。\n开辟你自己的道路。别循着任何人走过的足迹。

column5: I shake my head, unsure of how to react.{w}\nThis world didn't belong to The Triumvirate. But not to us, either.{w}\nWe were simply their creation, given free will by The Monarchy.
column6: 我摇了摇头，不知该如何回应。{w}\n这个世界不属于三人执政团。但也不属于我们。{w}\n我们不过是他们的造物，是王权赋予了自由意志。

column5: This seems to have been a conquest meant to reclaim their world.{w}\nThey may not be alive to see it happen, but we should rule it like they did.{w}\nI have the blade, too, and I was from Valinorth. I always looked toward the future.
column6: 这似乎是一场旨在夺回他们世界的征伐。{w}\n他们或许无法活着看到这一天，但我们应该像他们那样统治它。{w}\n我也有那把刃，我也出自瓦利诺斯。我一向放眼未来。

column5: All of those things considered, I was uniquely qualified to rule in their stead.{w}\nI couldn't just use everything they gave me, and then throw away their ideals.
column6: 考虑到这一切，我格外有资格代替他们来统治。{w}\n我不能白白利用他们给我的一切，然后抛弃他们的理想。

column5: You don't understand...!
column6: 你不明白……！

column5: He throws the book aside, and pins me back against the wall.{w}\nI stand strong, meeting his gaze — almost as if issuing a direct challenge.{w}\nHis grip is strong, and I can tell he's really passionate about this subject.
column6: 他把书丢到一边，将我摁在墙上。{w}\n我站得笔直，迎上他的目光——几乎像是在直接挑衅。{w}\n他抓得很紧，看得出他对此事真的很有激情。

column5: If you let them control your actions, then you'll never truly be free.\nNo matter who you align with, you'll inherit ideals that harm like poison.\nYou need to look to the past, not the future. Avoid the mistakes they made.
column6: 如果你任由他们掌控你的行为，那你就永远不会真正自由。\n无论你与谁结盟，你都会继承像毒药一样有害的理想。\n你需要回望过去，而不是展望未来。避开他们犯下的错误。

column5: That's what I did, and look where it brought me.\nStanding before you, able to think of little else.\nI just don't want to see you fall. You're {i}better{/i}.
column6: 我就是这么做的，看看它把我带到了哪里。\n站在你面前，除了你几乎什么都想不了。\n我只是不想看到你倒下。你{i}更好{/i}。

column5: Better than The Triumvirate. Better than The Monarchy.\nYou're the only person that's ever treated me like I mattered.\nI'm not a slave to you. I'm not just some \"means to an end\".
column6: 比三人执政团更好。比王权更好。\n你是唯一一个把我当回事的人。\n我不是你的奴隶。我不只是个“达成目的的手段”。

column5: He still has me pinned against the wall, and I feel him tremble.{w}\nA few moments later, he lets go of me. But I pull him back in.{w}\nHe looks away from me, and I can feel his breath against my neck.
column6: 他仍旧把我摁在墙上，我感觉到他在发抖。{w}\n片刻之后，他松开了我。但我又把他拉了回来。{w}\n他把目光移开，我能感觉到他的呼吸拂过我的颈项。

column5: I kept telling myself that you weren't giving me any special treatment.\nI wanted to believe that you'd extend the same courtesies to anybody.\nBut then you got me those writing utensils, and I became so confused.
column6: 我不断告诉自己，你并没有给我什么特殊待遇。\n我想相信，你对任何人都会给予同样的礼遇。\n可后来你送我那些书写工具，我就彻底困惑了。

column5: I can feel a rage well up within him as he speaks.{w}\nWithout warning, he punches the wall beside me with a loud grunt.{w}\nHowever, one of his hands still rests gently at my side. He's conflicted.
column6: 他开口时，我能感觉到他体内涌起一股怒火。{w}\n毫无预兆地，他低吼一声，一拳砸在我身旁的墙上。{w}\n然而，他的另一只手仍轻轻搭在我身侧。他内心在挣扎。

column5: I hate that I can't stop thinking about you.\nI hate that I care more about your future than my own!
column6: 我恨自己无法停止想你。\n我恨自己在意你的未来胜过在意自己的！

column5: He strikes the wall once more, and then looks me dead in the eyes.{w}\nHis second hand returns to my side, and he pins me against the wall again.
column6: 他又砸了一下墙，然后死死地盯住我的眼睛。{w}\n他第二只手也回到我身侧，再次把我摁在墙上。

column5: I hate you...
column6: 我恨你……

column5: And a moment later, our lips press together.{w}\nI rest my hands on his sides, and then quickly turn the tables.{w}\nSpinning both of us around, I press him against the wall as we continue to kiss.
column6: 片刻之后，我们的唇贴在了一起。{w}\n我双手放在他身侧，随即迅速扭转局面。{w}\n我把我们两人转了个身，将他压在墙上，继续亲吻。

column5: As we take it further, Sovy emits noises that enforce his confusion and anger.{w}\nWe move to different surfaces — the table, and then the bed — as we continue.{w}\nIt felt as natural as it did abrupt, and this is how we spent the rest of our time together.
column6: 随着我们更进一步，索维发出种种声音，印证着他的困惑与愤怒。{w}\n我们换了几处地方——先是桌子，然后是床——继续着一切。{w}\n这一切既自然而然又来得突然，我们就这样度过了余下的时光。

column5: After a few moments of silence, he releases his grip on my body.{w}\nHe turns around, and looks away, as if he's ashamed at his actions.
column6: 沉默片刻之后，他松开了对我的钳制。{w}\n他转过身去，把目光移开，仿佛为自己的行为感到羞愧。

column5: I apologize, [firstname].\nI let my emotions get the better of me.\nAround you, I feel almost free to express them.
column6: 我道歉，[firstname]。\n我让情绪占了上风。\n在你身边，我几乎能自由地表达它们。

column5: I tell him not to worry, and I accept his apology.{w}\nHis allegiance, at its core, has always been to the world.{w}\nHe just wanted me to take care of it when it was in my hands.
column6: 我告诉他别担心，并接受了他的道歉。{w}\n他内心深处的忠诚，始终是献给这个世界的。{w}\n他只是希望我在世界交到我手中时，能好好照顾它。

column5: It's probably best if we forget this ever happened.\nI'll get back to what I was doing, and see you in the atrium.\nAfter all, we don't have much time left. We've come to the end.
column6: 我们最好就当这一切从未发生过。\n我要回去忙我的事了，中庭见。\n毕竟，我们剩下的时间不多了。我们已经走到尽头了。

column5: Before he leaves, I make sure to tell him that he made a good point.{w}\nIn the future, if his views ever differ, I request that he feel free to speak up.{w}\nA ruler needs some people to help them walk the right path — myself included.
column6: 在他离开之前，我特意告诉他，他说得很有道理。{w}\n将来，如果他的看法不同，我希望他能畅所欲言。{w}\n一位统治者需要有人帮他们走在正道上——包括我自己。

column5: Very well.
column6: 很好。

column5: With a nod, he leaves the room.{w}\nI pick up the book he threw, and put it back on the shelf.{w}\nAs time goes by, I feel the weight of the world rest upon my shoulders.
column6: 他点点头，离开了房间。{w}\n我捡起他丢下的书，放回书架。{w}\n随着时间流逝，我感到整个世界都压在了我的肩上。

column5: After we won — if we won — the real work would begin.{w}\nWe had to win the people over, and figure out how we'd handle Alestia.{w}\nBecause of Sovy, I'm now filled with doubt. Was there any {i}right{/i} way to rule the world?
column6: 等我们赢了——如果我们赢了——真正的工作才会开始。{w}\n我们必须赢得民心，并想清楚该如何治理阿莱斯蒂亚。{w}\n因为索维，我如今满是疑虑。统治这个世界真的存在{i}正确{/i}的方式吗？

column5: I don't know. I really don't.{w}\nAll we can do is avoid mistakes of the past.{w}\nBut that only paves the way for us to make {i}new{/i} mistakes.
column6: 我不知道。我真的不知道。{w}\n我们能做的，只是避开过去的错误。{w}\n但那只会为我们犯下{i}新{/i}错误铺平道路。

column5: All I could do, was hope that these new mistakes didn't harm the world.{w}\nI meant well — but at the end of the day — that doesn't really count for much.{w}\nThe Triumvirate and The Monarchy both went well; and look at what happened.
column6: 我唯一能做的，就是希望这些新错误不会伤害这个世界。{w}\n我本意是好的——但归根结底——那其实算不上什么。{w}\n三人执政团和王权的本意也都是好的；看看后来发生了什么。

column5: We enter the tavern, and make sure to stick close together.{w}\nIt was packed, noisy, and the patrons seemed pretty rowdy.{w}\nI make sure to stick by Ulric in case something breaks out.
column6: 我们走进酒馆，紧紧挨在一起。{w}\n这里人满为患，吵吵嚷嚷，顾客们似乎相当喧闹。{w}\n我紧跟着乌尔里克，以防出什么事。

column5: It looks just like I remember it.\nAll these years — and nothing has changed.\nI guess there's no use trying to change perfection.
column6: 它看起来就和我记忆里一模一样。\n这么多年过去了——什么都没变。\n我想，试图改变完美的东西是没用的。

column5: Yes. It looks much like it did in our time, as well.\nIf memory serves, Alarinthia is home to a unique wine.\n[firstname]. If you have a drink, we would suggest that.
column6: 没错。它和我们那个年代的样子也差不多。\n如果我没记错，阿拉林西亚出产一种独特的酒。\n[firstname]。如果你要喝点什么，我们推荐那个。

column5: Wow, he actually knows what he's talking about.\nI'm buying a few bottles to bring back to the mainland.\nThe climate of Alarinthia affects the taste of everything.
column6: 哇，他居然真知道自己在说什么。\n我要买几瓶带回大陆去。\n阿拉林西亚的气候影响着一切事物的味道。

column5: Some in a good way, and some in a bad way.\nI won't bore you with the details, but the wine is great.\nLet's find Vivien and get everything started, shall we?
column6: 有些是好的影响，有些是坏的。\n我就不拿细节烦你了，但那酒确实很棒。\n我们去找薇薇安，把一切办起来吧？

column5: We all nod to one another, and venture deeper into the tavern.{w}\nIt's an open place, with no doors. I can see right outside to the market.{w}\nIt makes things noisy — almost unbearably so — but I'll have to deal with it.
column6: 我们互相点了点头，往酒馆深处走去。{w}\n这是个敞开的地方，没有门。我能直接看到外面的集市。{w}\n这让这里很吵闹——几乎吵得让人受不了——但我只好忍着。

column5: We approach the bar. I assume Ulric is going to ask after Vivien.{w}\nI can't even see Drakeor. I look around and notice a bunch of eyes on us.{w}\nPart of me starts to wonder if this {i}was{/i} a trap. Something feels odd.
column6: 我们走近吧台。我以为乌尔里克会去打听薇薇安。{w}\n我连德雷库的影子都没看到。我环顾四周，注意到许多目光落在我们身上。{w}\n我内心开始怀疑，这{i}是不是{/i}个陷阱。总觉得有些不对劲。

column5: A man sneaks up from behind us, and stands between me and Ulric.{w}\nHe has a drink in his hand, and he slams it down on the table.{w}\nSome of it spills on the bar. This man must be intoxicated.
column6: 一个男人从我们身后悄悄靠近，站到我和乌尔里克之间。{w}\n他手里端着一杯酒，重重地把它砸在桌上。{w}\n有些酒溅到了吧台上。这人一定是喝醉了。

column5: Hey, would you let me buy you a drink?\nSomething tells me you're not from around here.\nI know a lot about this place, if you need a tour guide.
column6: 嘿，能让我请你喝一杯吗？\n我总觉得你不是本地人。\n如果你需要向导，我对这地方知道得可多了。

column5: Before I can answer, Ulric gently pushes them away.
column6: 还没等我回答，乌尔里克就轻轻地把他推开了。

column5: Look, we don't have time for any antics.\nBut if you know where Vivien is, we could use some help.\nYou're right about us being foreigners. We've come a long way.
column6: 听着，我们没时间陪你胡闹。\n但如果你知道薇薇安在哪，我们倒需要些帮忙。\n你说对了，我们是外地人。我们走了很远的路。

column5: Oh, you're looking for Vivien...?\nWhy didn't you say so? Follow me.
column6: 哦，你们在找薇薇安……？\n怎么不早说？跟我来。

column5: Ulric and I stare at each other, at unease.
column6: 我和乌尔里克不安地对视了一眼。

column5: We'd rather stay here, if you don't mind.\nFollowing strangers isn't the best idea.
column6: 如果你不介意，我们宁愿留在这儿。\n跟着陌生人走可不是什么好主意。

column5: Alright, alright. I'll be right back.\nNormally, I wouldn't do this. But I trust you.\nHave I seen you before...? You look familiar.
column6: 好吧，好吧。我马上回来。\n一般情况下我不会这么做。但我信得过你们。\n我以前见过你吗……？你看起来很眼熟。

column5: No. Now please leave us be.\nDon't bother us again unless you have Vivien.\nI'll ask the barkeep in the meantime. Maybe they know.
column6: 没有。现在请你别打扰我们了。\n除非你带着薇薇安，否则别再烦我们。\n我先去问问酒保。也许他们知道。

column5: The mystery man nods and walks away from us.{w}\nI doubt he'd be coming back. He was probably a scammer.{w}\nIs there something about us that marks us as easy targets...?
column6: 那个神秘的男人点点头，走开了。{w}\n我怀疑他不会回来了。他多半是个骗子。{w}\n我们身上有什么东西让我们看起来像好骗的目标吗……？

column5: Now, I guess I'll start—
column6: 那么，我想我该开始——

column5: Before he can continue, Drakeor sneaks up behind us.
column6: 还没等他说下去，德雷库从我们身后悄悄出现。

column5: Your manners could use some work, Ulric.
column6: 你的礼貌还有待改进，乌尔里克。

column5: I use my manners on worthwhile people.
column6: 我只对值得的人讲礼貌。

column5: And Vivien isn't one of them...?\nI saw how you just shoved him away.
column6: 薇薇安不算是其中之一……？\n我看见你刚才是怎么把他推开的。

column5: Wait, what...?\nVivien is a man?
column6: 等等，什么……？\n薇薇安是个男人？
